stories.description: `ChartLegend`'s `valueFormat` resolves as a SET across every item (#250) — with an object spec, every value shares the same abbreviate/decimals decision instead of compacting independently.

stories.name: Metric Card Object Spec
stories.description: `MetricCard`'s `valueFormat` (`@elabs-ai/components-ui`) accepts the same object-spec shape as the chart engine — a deliberate twin (`packages/ui/src/lib/compact-number.ts`), since `ui` cannot import `charts`.

charts/funnelchart.name: FunnelChart
charts/funnelchart.title: Charts/FunnelChart
charts/funnelchart.summary: Stage-by-stage drop-off through an ordered pipeline.

intent.purpose: Stage-by-stage drop-off through an ordered pipeline.
antiPatterns: Using it for unordered categories — a funnel asserts a sequence; unordered data belongs in a bar chart.
Encoding stage identity by colour alone — label each stage; colour is not a legend.
Hiding the absolute counts behind percentages only — a funnel without its base number cannot be judged.
dataShapes: a sequential process with drop-off between stages
intent.avoidWhen: the stages are not sequential, or there is no drop-off story to tell

props.name: plotHeight
props.description: The plot's own height (ADR 0039): px, or `{ aspect }` (width ÷ height), optionally per breakpoint.

props.name: hoveredIndex
props.description: Controlled hover state — index of the hovered segment

props.name: onHoverChange
props.description: Callback when hover state changes

props.name: staggerDelay
props.description: Stagger delay between segments in seconds. Default 0.12

props.name: enterTransition
props.description: Framer Motion transition for segment enter animation

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between segments in pixels. Default 4

props.name: renderPattern
props.description: Render a visx pattern definition. Receives a unique `id` string per segment and the resolved `color`. Return a `<PatternLines>` (or any visx pattern) inside an SVG `<defs>`. The component will use `fill="url(#id)"` on the innermost ring while keeping outer halo rings as solid color.

props.name: onDatapointClick
props.description: Drill-down (#349). Fires when a stage is activated by pointer OR keyboard. Setting it mounts a keyboard-operable target layer OUTSIDE the aria-hidden SVG — one tab stop, arrow keys to traverse. Unset changes nothing.

props.name: copyValueOnActivate
props.description: Put the datapoint's exact value on the clipboard when it is activated — the recovery path for a compact axis label. Default `false`; a chart with no interaction props still renders byte-identical DOM. A consumer-supplied `onDatapointClick` always wins.

props.name: datapointLabel
props.description: Override the accessible name of each keyboard drill-down target (#349).

props.name: maxInteractiveDatapoints
props.description: Dev-warning threshold on the number of keyboard targets. Default 500 (#349).

props.name: accessibleLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the chart region (announces to AT on focus).

props.name: accessibleDescription
props.description: Supplemental description read by AT (e.g. stage names + values).

props.name: edges
props.description: Edge style for the funnel segments. Default "curved"

props.name: labelLayout
props.description: Controls how segment labels (value, percentage, stage name) are arranged. - "spread": Value/percentage/label are spread apart (top/center/bottom for horizontal, left/center/right for vertical). This is the default. - "grouped": All label items stack together in a tight group. When "grouped", use `labelOrientation` and `labelAlign` for full control.

props.name: labelOrientation
props.description: Stack direction of the label group. Only applies when `labelLayout="grouped"`. - "vertical": Items stack top-to-bottom. Default for horizontal funnels. - "horizontal": Items stack left-to-right. Default for vertical funnels.

props.name: labelAlign
props.description: Where the label group sits within the segment cell. - "center" (default), "start", "end" For horizontal funnel: start=top, end=bottom. For vertical funnel: start=left, end=right.

props.name: showConversion
props.description: Stage-to-stage conversion — the % of the PREVIOUS stage's value, rendered as a small opaque plate (lieflat L13's "62% GET THROUGH" margin note — the number funnel readers actually want, distinct from the existing `showPercentage` badge which is always "% of the first stage"). The plate carries its own ground/ink pair (like `SegmentLabel`'s percentage pill), so it stays legible on any band fill in any theme — see #239. - `"between"` places one annotation at the boundary between each pair of adjacent segments. - `"margin"` stacks all transitions in a column near the funnel's leading edge (left edge for horizontal, top edge for vertical). - `false` (default) renders nothing — an existing `FunnelChart` with no `showConversion` prop is unaffected. When set, the interactive stage overlay (hover/click target) also gets a native `title` tooltip reading "N% of previous stage · M% of first stage".

stories.name: With Accessible Label
stories.description: Accessible variant — announces label + description to screen readers on focus.

stories.name: Conversion — between stages
stories.description: Stage-to-stage conversion (lieflat L13) at every boundary — the number funnel readers actually want, distinct from `showPercentage`'s "% of the first stage" badge. Reconciles with the data: 4,800/12,000 = 40%, 2,100/4,800 = 44%, 840/2,100 = 40%.

stories.name: Conversion — margin
stories.description: Same conversion numbers, stacked in the left margin (lieflat L13's "62% GET THROUGH").

stories.name: Drilldown
stories.description: Click a stage — or Tab in and press Enter — to drill into it.

charts/gantt.name: Gantt
charts/gantt.title: Charts/Gantt
charts/gantt.summary: Schedule grid — tasks as bars over time, with a task table beside them.

intent.purpose: Schedule grid — tasks as bars over time, with a task table beside them.
antiPatterns: Mutating task dates inside the component on drag — Gantt is emit-only; the app owns the model (D5).
Bar labels that rely on the bar fill for contrast — check the label against the bar color in every theme.
Rendering the grid without `loading` while rows are still fetching — skeleton rows must hold the layout.
dataShapes: tasks or phases across a timeline, with dependencies between them
intent.avoidWhen: it is not really scheduled work — a dumbbell chart shows a single before and after

props.name: tasks
props.description: Task data.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: Row height override (px). Defaults to density-derived value.

props.name: viewMode
props.description: Controlled tick granularity. Accepts any {@link GanttTimeUnit}.

props.name: defaultViewMode
props.description: Initial tick granularity. Default `"week"`. Pass `"auto"` to derive the finest readable unit from the data's own span (see {@link pickGanttTimeUnit}) — the default stays `"week"` so no existing surface changes granularity (#360).

props.name: onViewModeChange
props.description: Emitted when the granularity changes. **Migration (#360):** the parameter widened from `GanttViewMode` to {@link GanttTimeUnit}. Under `strictFunctionTypes` a handler *explicitly* annotated `(mode: GanttViewMode) => void` no longer assigns — annotate it `GanttTimeUnit`, or drop the annotation (the common inferred form `onViewModeChange={(mode) => …}` is unaffected). Runtime behaviour is unchanged: without `viewModes` the toolbar still only emits the four calendar presets.

props.name: viewModes
props.description: Units offered by the toolbar's segmented control. Default `["day", "week", "month", "quarter"]`.

props.name: onTaskMove
props.type: (id: string, start: Date, end: Date) => void

props.name: pointerDrag
props.description: Enable pointer drag (move / resize-edge / create-link), in addition to the always-available keyboard editing. Drag fires the SAME emit-only `onTaskMove` / `onTaskResize` / `onDependencyCreate` — the task model is never mutated (D5). Defaults to `true` when any of those callbacks is provided; pass `false` to force keyboard-only.

props.name: columns
props.description: Left-pane columns. The first column hosts the task name + tree affordances.

props.name: scales
props.description: Stacked timescale rows. Overrides the `viewMode`-derived default.

props.name: labelPosition
props.description: Bar-label placement. Default `"inside"`.

props.name: highlightTime
props.description: Returns a semantic `bg-*` class for a vertical band at `date`, else undefined.

props.name: markers
props.description: Vertical annotation markers (themed line + optional label at a date).

props.name: renderBar
props.description: Custom LEAF-bar renderer (escape hatch). Your node fills the bar rect and is `aria-hidden`; the button shell (selection, keyboard editing, pointer drag, tooltip, baseline) is preserved. Summary brackets and milestones keep their built-in rendering. Omit for the default type-driven rendering.

props.name: taskTypes
props.description: Custom task types (color/shape) selected per task via `GanttTask.type`.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP-47 locale for the default date formatting (passed to `Intl`).

props.name: formatDate
props.description: Override date formatting entirely (P2). Defaults to `Intl` + `locale`.

props.name: pixelsPerDay
props.description: Controlled pixels-per-day (continuous zoom). Overrides the view-mode preset.

props.name: defaultPixelsPerDay
props.description: Initial pixels-per-day for uncontrolled zoom (enables Ctrl/⌘ + wheel out of the box).

props.name: onPixelsPerDayChange
props.description: Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zoom emits the proposed pixels-per-day.

props.name: zoomBounds
props.description: Override the span-derived zoom clamp (see {@link computeGanttZoomBounds}). Both bounds are in pixels-per-day, at every granularity (#360).

props.name: sort
props.description: Controlled sort descriptors (drive the header sort indicators).

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Header click on a `sortable` column emits the next sort state.

props.name: onColumnResize
props.description: Header-edge drag on a `resizable` column emits the proposed width.

props.name: labelColumnWidth
props.description: Left pane width (px). Default 240. Ignored when `columns` is set (widths sum).

props.name: loading
props.description: When true, renders a built-in shimmer loading state (Skeleton rows in both panes) instead of the task tree and canvas. Use while data is in flight.

stories.name: Multi Column Grid
stories.description: Multi-column left grid (P1) — name stays in the accessible Tree; the data columns are an aria-hidden overlay.

stories.name: Grouped Timescale
stories.description: Three stacked timescale rows via an explicit `scales` array (P1).

stories.name: Label Position End
stories.description: Bar labels placed at the END so short bars/milestones stay legible (P1).

stories.name: Label Hidden
stories.description: Bar labels hidden — relies on the task grid / tooltip / aria-label (P1).

stories.name: Weekend Highlight
stories.description: Weekend highlight bands via `highlightTime` (P1) — token-backed classes only.

stories.name: Drag To Edit
stories.description: Pointer drag (P1, emit-only) — drag a bar body to move, drag the edges to resize; selecting a bar reveals the link handle (drag onto another bar to emit `onDependencyCreate`). The play test performs a real move drag.

stories.name: Baseline Track
stories.description: Planned-vs-actual baseline track under each bar (P2).

stories.name: Gap Bands
stories.description: Idle-time bands (P2, #221) — a hatched fill spanning a row's `gaps` entries, reusing the ADR 0011 series-pattern mechanism UNCONDITIONALLY (not gated behind high decoration): the meaning ("idle") must not rest on colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1), so the hatch shape is always the second channel. Hover the band, or inspect its `aria-label`, for the accessible name — the caller's `label` when given, else a generated description.

stories.name: Annotations
stories.description: Vertical annotation markers (P2) — themed lines + label chips.

stories.name: Custom Task Types
stories.description: Custom task types (P2) — color + shape per type.

stories.name: Inside Label Contrast
stories.description: Inside-label contrast target (#259) — bars on the lowest-contrast fills (destructive, warning, chart-3) plus a consumer-supplied `taskTypes` color, so the on-bar label pill can be checked across every theme (light/dark) on the fills most likely to fail.

stories.name: Custom Bar Render
stories.description: Custom bar renderer (P2) — escape hatch; consumer owns the leaf-bar visual.

stories.name: Localized
stories.description: Localized dates (P2) — `locale` drives the default Intl formatting.

stories.name: Zoomable
stories.description: Continuous zoom (P2) — Ctrl/⌘ + wheel emits a controlled `cellWidth`.

stories.name: Sortable Columns
stories.description: Sortable + resizable columns (P2) — emit-only; the consumer sorts/sizes.

stories.name: Full Featured
stories.description: Everything together — grid + grouped timescale + weekend bands + editing.

stories.name: Agent Run Trace
stories.description: Sub-day time units (#360) — the same `Gantt` over a **12-second** agent run. `defaultViewMode="auto"` derives the finest readable unit from the data's own span (here: seconds); the toolbar offers `Millisecond / Second / Minute`, and Ctrl/⌘ + scroll zooms continuously. `pixelsPerDay` keeps its exact meaning — pixels per 86 400 000 ms — at every granularity.

stories.name: Millisecond Trace
stories.description: Sub-SECOND granularity — a 40 ms dispatch trace with millisecond ticks (`fractionalSecondDigits`). Same component, same `pixelsPerDay` semantics.

charts/gauge.name: Gauge
charts/gauge.title: Charts/Gauge
charts/gauge.summary: Single-value dial against a known range — a KPI with an explicit ceiling.

intent.purpose: Single-value dial against a known range — a KPI with an explicit ceiling.
antiPatterns: A gauge for a value with no meaningful maximum — that is a MetricCard, not a dial.
A gauge per KPI in a grid — a row of dials reads worse than a MetricGrid; use one for the headline only.
Encoding the threshold by colour alone — pair the band with a label or a tick.
dataShapes: a single value against a target or threshold bands

props.name: value
props.description: Fill level 0–100

props.name: totalNotches
props.description: Number of arc notches

props.name: spacing
props.description: Percentage of the arc reserved for gaps between notches

props.name: notchCornerRadius
props.description: Corner fillet radius for each notch corner (pixels). **0** = sharp corners; higher values read more rounded; geometry clamps so large values approach a capsule / near-circular silhouette.

props.name: uniformWidth
props.description: `true` = rectangular notches; `false` = tapered toward the center

props.name: activeGradient
props.description: Override the active-notch gradient with two explicit hex stops to interpolate along the arc. When omitted (the default), notches use the theme chart palette (`--chart-1` → `--chart-5`) — no hardcoded colors.

props.name: inactiveGradient
props.description: When `useGradient` is true, inactive notch colors interpolate between these hex stops. Defaults to {@link activeGradient} when omitted.

props.name: centerValue
props.description: Value passed to {@link PieCenterShell} / NumberFlow

props.name: inactiveFill
props.description: Inactive / track notch fill — CSS color or `url(#patternId)` (define patterns in `children`).

props.name: activeFill
props.description: Active notch fill — CSS color or `url(#patternId)`. When set, overrides solid / gradient active fills for that layer.

props.name: inactiveFillOpacity
props.description: SVG `fill-opacity` for inactive / track notches (0–1). Default **1** — the track rung is already tuned lighter than the hairline ink.

props.name: activeFillOpacity
props.description: SVG `fill-opacity` for active notches (0–1). Default **1**.

props.name: children
props.description: `PatternLines`, gradients, etc. — rendered inside `<defs>` (same convention as `PieChart` children).

props.name: width
props.description: Explicit pixel size. When omitted, the gauge fills its parent; give the parent a size (e.g. `min-w-[300px]` + aspect box) for responsive layouts.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: Minimum width (px) when using the built-in responsive wrapper. Default 300

props.name: notchLengthPercent
props.description: Radial depth of notches as a **%** of the built-in default (outer 42% / inner 28% of `size`). **100** = full length; lower values pull the inner edge toward the outer arc. Clamped **5–100**.

props.name: enterTransition
props.description: Framer Motion transition for notch enter animation (opacity / scale).

props.name: enterStaggerScale
props.description: Scales notch stagger delays relative to default timing (1 = reference).

props.name: milestones
props.description: Milestone values (0–100) marked with a small dot on the dial and a halo-text number just **outside** the notch band, joined by a short dotted leader — e.g. `[25, 50, 75, 100]` (lieflat F11). Setting `milestones` reserves a small radial margin so the leader + label never clip the gauge's own box; a `Gauge` with `milestones` unset renders its pre-existing, unaffected geometry. #248.

props.name: remainingLabel
props.description: Caption rendered under the center value/label. Receives the number of notches remaining (`totalNotches - activeNotches`) and returns the caption text — e.g. `(remaining) => \`${remaining} ticks to go\`` renders as "27 TICKS TO GO" (lieflat F11; the caption is rendered upper-cased via CSS, so pass ordinary sentence case). Unset (default) renders no caption.

props.name: target
props.description: A radial tick crossing the notch band at this value (0–100) — e.g. a quarterly target. Reuses the same value→angle mapping as notches/ milestones. Unset (default) renders no tick and the dial's geometry is unaffected.

props.name: thresholds
props.description: Short outer-rim ticks (furniture — `--chart-grid`, `CHART_HAIRLINE_WIDTH`) marking named bands (e.g. `{ value: 75, label: "Good" }`). No colour zones — colour is not status here, only the accessible text names the band a value falls in. Unset (default) renders no ticks.

props.name: labels
props.description: Overrides the shipped English words the composed accessible text uses (`target`).

stories.name: Default
stories.description: Notched arc gauge, no milestones — the pre-existing (unaffected) default.

stories.name: With milestones (F11)
stories.description: Milestone dots at 25/50/75/100 with a "N ticks to go" caption — lieflat F11. `totalNotches={40}` and `value={32}` reproduce the finding's own example (`32% ⇒ 13 active notches ⇒ 27 remaining` → "27 TICKS TO GO").

stories.name: Milestones Only
stories.description: Milestones alone, no caption — the two additive props are independent.

stories.name: Long Caption
stories.description: A caption roughly 2x the `WithMilestones` fixture's length (#248). It must wrap inside the donut hole rather than growing across the tick arc.

stories.name: With Target
stories.description: A radial tick crossing the notch band at `target` — a quarterly goal.

stories.name: With Thresholds
stories.description: Short outer-rim ticks naming bands — colour is not status here, only the accessible text names the band.

stories.name: Target And Thresholds
stories.description: Both together — the accessible description composes to "72 of 100, target 80, band Good".

stories.name: Accessible Name
stories.description: `accessibleLabel`/`accessibleDescription` (#290) — a named, focusable figure.

charts/heatmapchart.name: HeatmapChart
charts/heatmapchart.title: Charts/HeatmapChart
charts/heatmapchart.summary: Two discrete dimensions × one value — weekday × hour, product × region, or a year of days.

intent.purpose: Two discrete dimensions × one value — weekday × hour, product × region, or a year of days.

stateTokens.cell: value → an ordered ramp step (--chart-seq-*, --chart-div-*, --chart-mono-* via resolvePalette)
stateTokens.empty: null or 0 → a QuietDot pinprick in --chart-foreground-muted, not a hole
stateTokens.peak: the highlighted cell → a dashed PeakRing in --chart-foreground
stateTokens.loading: loading → the same grid as skeleton cells in --muted

antiPatterns: steps: 0 (the continuous ramp) when the reader must compare exact values — opacity is not countable; keep the stepped ramp or turn showValues on.
emptyValue="blank" on data that contains real zeroes — a measured zero then looks identical to a missing row, which is the one thing the pinprick exists to prevent.
Forcing the calendar variant into a narrow box (overflow-hidden, a tall aspectRatio) — it enforces a minimum width and scrolls on purpose; squeezed day cells fall below the 24px target size.
Leaning on the darkest ramp step to say "this is the peak" — colour alone; highlight draws the ring, and a diverging palette needs showValues or its negative hatch for sign.
dataShapes: two categorical axes (weekday by hour, for example) with one numeric value per cell — ticket volume, event counts; many small cells favour mode="dot" over the default cell fill
one measure per calendar day over several months, as variant="calendar"
intent.avoidWhen: more than about 10 columns of continuous data, or exact cell values matter more than the pattern

stories.name: Matrix
stories.description: The punch card: 7 weekdays × 24 hours, 168 cells, five countable shade steps (L16). Measured zeroes draw a pinprick, keyed “zero” in the legend; a cell with no value would draw an outline instead (see `ZeroVersusMissing`).

stories.name: Matrix With Values
stories.description: G20: a small enough matrix that every cell can carry its own number.

stories.name: Legend Range Labels
stories.description: `legendLabels="ranges"` (RM-118): a `from–to` label under every swatch instead of just the strip's `lo`/`hi` endpoints — lets a reader place a cell in its step without hovering it. Five countable steps (the default), so the legend prints five swatches and five range labels.

stories.name: Dot Heat
stories.description: F10: the value is the dot's AREA, not its radius — so a doubled number draws a dot √2 wider, never twice as wide. The shade tracks the same ramp, so the two encodings agree instead of competing.

stories.name: Calendar
stories.description: L17: a year of deploys as 53 week columns × 7 weekday rows, with a month label above the week that holds each month's first Monday. A weekend with no deploy is a pinprick, not a gap.

stories.name: Diverging
stories.description: Week-over-week change. A diverging ramp is lightness-symmetric by construction, so in greyscale a `+18` and a `-18` are the same colour — this chart therefore always carries a second, non-hue channel for sign: the value labels are on by default, and turning them off hatches the negative cells instead (see `DivergingHatched`).

stories.name: Diverging — hatched (labels off)
stories.description: The same data with the labels off — sign then rides a 45° hatch.

stories.name: Zero versus missing
stories.description: Zero is not missing. With the labels off, a measured `0` is a pinprick and a cell with no value is a hairline outline — two shapes, two legend keys, so a reader can tell “flat” from “never measured” without colour or numbers.

stories.name: Loading
stories.description: The layout-shaped skeleton: the same grid, so nothing shifts when data lands.

stories.name: Empty
stories.description: No rows at all — an empty state, never an empty grid pretending to be data. It fills the same 16 / 9 plot box a loaded chart does, so a filter that empties the grid does not collapse the page under the reader’s cursor.

stories.name: Drilldown
stories.description: Click a cell to drill into it. The pointer path activates the CELL itself; the layer's `<button>`s are `pointer-events: none` on purpose — they exist so a keyboard user reaches what a mouse user can click, without adding a second hit target over the chart. So this story clicks the mark, and `KeyboardDrilldown` drives the buttons.

stories.name: Keyboard Drilldown
stories.description: The same drill-down with the keyboard only: one tab stop for the whole grid, arrows to traverse it, Enter to activate.

stories.name: Selection states
stories.description: `selectionStates` paints the host’s tri-state on cells (keyed on the column category): selected marks carry a compound foreground/background outline, excluded marks dim AND carry a full-opacity dashed frame, so the three states stay distinguishable in greyscale.

stories.name: End Labels With Key Fallback
stories.description: Wide: each series is named at its line end, and the two peaks carry their value. Below 480 px the names move into a key row above the plot.

stories.name: Key Row When Narrow
stories.description: The same chart in a 380 px column: the names sit in a key row above the plot.

stories.name: Default And Opt Out
stories.description: No label props at all: with two or more named series, each series names itself at the line end by default. The second chart opts out with `seriesLabel="none"`.

stories.name: ${name} College
stories.description: One series, no label props: the chart title already names it, so the default paints no end label. `seriesLabel="end"` on the Line would paint one.

stories.name: Labelled Scatter
stories.description: Thirty labelled schools. `mode: "auto"` keeps one label per 6000 px² of plot, largest borrower count first, so a narrow chart paints fewer names; every dropped name is restated `sr-only`.

stories.name: Bar Values Auto And Hover
stories.description: `showValues={{ placement: "auto" }}`: inside a bar long enough to hold the label, outside a short one. The second chart prints only the hovered bar.

charts/linechart.name: LineChart
charts/linechart.title: Charts/LineChart
charts/linechart.summary: Trend over a continuous (usually time) axis.

intent.purpose: Trend over a continuous (usually time) axis.
antiPatterns: A LineChart over unordered categories — a line asserts continuity; use a BarChart.
More than ~5 series in one plot — past the chart-1…chart-5 palette the series stop being distinguishable; facet instead.
Distinguishing series by color alone — add markers or direct labels for non-color users.
dataShapes: one or more measures over continuous time, where the trend itself is the point
intent.avoidWhen: more than about 8 series — use a stream area chart or a composed chart

props.name: data
props.description: Data array - each item should have a date field and numeric values

props.name: xDataKey
props.description: Key in data for the x-axis (date). Default: "date"

props.name: xScale
props.description: How `xDataKey` values are interpreted (#352). Default: `"time"`. - `"time"` — Date (or Date-coercible) x values on a time scale. - `"band"` — categorical x values (`"Turn 1"`, `"Step A"`), evenly spaced in first-seen order. Axis ticks, the ticker and the tooltip title all show your own value, not a formatted date. - `"linear"` — numeric x values spaced by magnitude. Omitting it keeps today's behaviour, except that a dataset whose x values are ALL non-Date-coercible degrades to `"band"` (with a dev warning) instead of collapsing.

props.name: margin
props.description: Chart margins

props.name: animationDuration
props.description: Animation duration in milliseconds. Default: 1100

props.name: animationEasing
props.description: CSS easing for clip-reveal. Default: cubic-bezier(0.85, 0, 0.15, 1)

props.name: revealOn
props.description: When the enter reveal is allowed to play (#175). `"mount"` (default) plays as soon as the chart renders — no change from today. `"inView"` holds the reveal at width 0 until this chart's own container scrolls to 30% visible.

props.name: replayOnClick
props.description: Clicking the chart body replays the enter reveal (#175). Default `false`.

props.name: aspectRatio
props.description: Aspect ratio as "width / height". Default: "2 / 1". Omit to fill a sized parent.

props.name: plotHeight
props.description: The plot's own height (ADR 0039): px, or `{ aspect }` (width ÷ height), optionally per breakpoint. Wins over `aspectRatio`, which stays an alias.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional class name for the container

props.name: status
props.description: Loading vs ready — drives chart phase and loading chrome. Default: `"ready"`.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: Centered shimmer label while loading.

props.name: yDomainTweenDuration
props.description: Animate y-domain over this duration (ms) on status transitions. Default: 500.

props.name: yDomainTween
props.description: Animate y-domain when status or target domain changes. Default: true

props.name: xDomain
props.description: Visible x-domain for brush zoom.

props.name: xDomainSlotCount
props.description: Full dataset length for x-scale padding when `xDomain` is set.

props.name: tweenYDomainOnXDomainChange
props.description: Tween y-domain when brush changes the visible x-range. Default: false

props.name: style
props.description: Inline container styles (e.g. fixed height for brush strip).

props.name: onPhaseChange
props.description: Fires when the internal chart phase changes (e.g. OG capture readiness).

props.name: children
props.description: Child components (Line, Grid, ChartTooltip, etc.)

props.name: onDatapointClick
props.description: Drill-down (#349). Fires when a datapoint is activated by pointer OR keyboard. Setting it mounts a keyboard-operable target layer OUTSIDE the aria-hidden SVG — one tab stop, arrow keys to traverse. Leaving it unset changes nothing: no extra DOM, no new focusables.

props.name: copyValueOnActivate
props.description: Put the datapoint's exact value on the clipboard when it is activated — the recovery path for a compact axis label. Default `false`; a chart with no interaction props still renders byte-identical DOM. A consumer-supplied `onDatapointClick` always wins.

props.name: datapointLabel
props.description: Override the accessible name of each keyboard drill-down target (#349).

props.name: maxInteractiveDatapoints
props.description: Dev-warning threshold on the number of keyboard targets. Default 500 (#349).

props.name: accessibleLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the chart region (announces to AT on focus).

props.name: accessibleDescription
props.description: Supplemental description read by AT (e.g. series names + value range).

props.name: nulls
props.description: Container-level default for a `Line`'s own `nulls` prop (RM-112). Unset — every `Line` keeps its own default (`"gap"`).

props.name: focusOnHover
props.description: Hovering (or, on touch, tapping) one series dims every other series to the shared selection-excluded opacity (RM-112, `dw-river.md` §2.3). Default false — today's behaviour.

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend engine (RM-118): `true` or a config object mounts `ChartLegend` beside the plot via `useContainerLegend`; `{ interactive: "toggle" }` hides a series and re-tweens the y-domain. Unset (default) renders NOTHING new (R1, moved into `useContainerLegend` itself) — RM-110's end labels stay the default multi-series key for `LineChart`.

props.name: dataKey
props.description: Key in data to use for y values

props.name: yAxisId
props.description: Y-scale group id (Recharts `yAxisId`). Default: `"left"`.

props.name: stroke
props.description: Stroke color. Default: var(--chart-line-primary)

props.name: strokeWidth
props.description: Stroke width. Default: 2.5. Set to 1 for a lieflat-style "hairline" line.

props.name: curve
props.description: Curve interpolation — a named alias (`"linear"` | `"monotone"` | `"natural"` | `"step"` | `"step-before"` | `"step-after"`, RM-112) or a raw `@visx/curve` factory. Default: `"monotone"`. `"natural"` (`curveNatural`, this package's pre-RM-112 default) is offered for parity only — Datawrapper's own guidance is to avoid natural/cardinal interpolation because it overshoots between two equal neighbours (`.claude/rules/charts.md` "Honesty").

props.name: animate
props.description: Whether to animate the line. Default: true

props.name: fadeEdges
props.description: Fade the line stroke toward transparent at the chart edges. - `true` fades both edges, `false` disables the fade entirely. - `"left"` / `"right"` fades only that side. Default: true

props.name: showHighlight
props.description: Whether to show highlight segment on hover. Default: true

props.name: showMarkers
props.description: Render scatter-style circle markers at each data point. Default: false

props.name: markers
props.description: Marker styling (same options as Scatter).

props.name: markerStyle
props.description: Per-point marker style — `"filled"` | `"hollow"` | `"none"`, decided per data point (RM-028). E.g. `(d) => (isWeekend(d.date) ? "hollow" : "filled")` — the lieflat "hollow dot = weekend, filled = weekday" idiom. Setting this renders a marker at every non-`"none"` point regardless of `showMarkers` — the per-point fill/stroke decision takes over from the shared marker style, while `markers.radius`/`ringGap`/`strokeWidth` still apply as the shared geometry. A hollow marker fills with `--chart-background` (the plot ground) so it stays theme-safe with no `dark:` override. Default: unset — no per-point styling, today's behaviour.

props.name: symbols
props.description: Placement/style wrapper over `showMarkers`/`markers` (RM-112, Datawrapper's line symbols: 8 shapes, first-and-last/all placement, filled/hollow style). Setting this turns markers on regardless of `showMarkers`. `placement` — `"all"` | `"ends"` | `"first"` | `"last"`, default `"ends"`. `style` — `"filled"` | `"hollow"`, default `"hollow"`. `shape`/`size` map onto `markers.shape`/`markers.radius`. Default unset: no symbols — today's behaviour, driven by `showMarkers`/`markers` alone.

props.name: nulls
props.description: How this line draws a non-numeric sample (RM-112). Overrides the container-level `LineChart nulls` default. Unset — read the container default, or `"gap"` with no container default (a visible break, never a silent zero — the pre-RM-112 default was the "zero" behaviour, kept as `nulls="zero"`).

props.name: outline
props.description: Paint a `--chart-background` halo stroke under the series stroke (Datawrapper's line outline, May 2024) so two crossing lines still read apart. `true` uses a 2px halo on each side; a number sets the halo width in px. Default `false` — no halo, today's behaviour.

props.name: labelPeaks
props.description: Label the top-k highest points on the line (RM-028) — lieflat's "top-2/top-3 peaks, enlarged and labelled" rule (L3 Barcode Lollipop). A bare number is the peak count at the default {@link DEFAULT_PEAK_MIN_GAP} -sample spacing; pass `{ count, minGap }` to override spacing. A peak within `minGap` samples of an already-picked (necessarily higher — peaks are picked highest-first) peak is skipped — "the barcode lesson: adjacent peaks must be forced apart" — so two close peaks label only the taller one. Uses the exported {@link spacedTopK} helper. Default: unset — no peak labels, today's behaviour.

props.name: name
props.description: Series display name — the text of its end label, key item and auto summary (RM-110). Default: `dataKey`.

props.name: seriesLabel
props.description: Where the series names itself (RM-110): `"end"` — a label at its last point (the chart reserves right margin for it); `"key"` — a swatch + name in a key row above the plot; `"none"`. Takes a `Responsive` value, e.g. `{ base: "end", narrow: "key" }`. Default: in a chart with two or more `Line`/`Area` series, a series whose `name` is set and differs from its `dataKey` gets `{ base: "end", narrow: "key" }` when a `ChartLegend` is composed, else `"end"`; every other series gets `"none"`. An explicit value always wins. Colliding end labels are nudged apart, or dropped and restated `sr-only`.

props.name: valueLabels
props.description: Automatic value labels (RM-110): `{ placement: "first" | "last" | "all" | "peaks", count?, outline?, matchColor?, format? }`. Placed with every other label through one collision pass — a label that cannot be placed is dropped and restated `sr-only`. `labelPeaks={n}` is the alias `{ placement: "peaks", count: n }` (exact, uncompacted numbers).

props.name: dashFromIndex
props.description: Data index from which the line stroke becomes dashed (inclusive). Useful for projecting incomplete periods, e.g. dashed from yesterday through today.

props.name: dashArray
props.description: Dash pattern for the tail segment when `dashFromIndex` is set. Default: "6,4"

props.name: dashStroke
props.description: Stroke color for the dashed tail (from `dashFromIndex` on) when it should read as a distinct series from the solid head — e.g. a projection tail in a quieter ink than the actual-data head. Default: `stroke` (today's behaviour — head and tail share one ink, differentiated by dash alone).

props.name: loading
props.description: Show the loading pulse overlay. Default: follows chart loading phase. Set `false` to disable even during loading.

props.name: loadingStroke
props.description: Stroke color for the loading pulse overlay. Default: var(--foreground)

props.name: loadingStrokeOpacity
props.description: Loading pulse stroke opacity. Default: 0.5

props.name: loadingPulseMode
props.description: Override pulse animation mode (loop / exit / enter).

props.name: onLoadingPulseCycleComplete
props.description: Called when a loop-mode pulse cycle completes.

props.name: seriesIndex
props.description: Override the series index used for pattern/dash/marker differentiation under high decoration — needed when a single-series chart must differ from a sibling chart, e.g. sparklines. Does NOT affect layout.

props.name: margin
props.description: Chart margins

props.name: stroke
props.description: Stroke color for the animated loading segment.

props.name: strokeOpacity
props.description: Stroke opacity for the animated loading segment. Default: 0.5

props.name: gridStroke
props.description: Grid line stroke (color and opacity via color-mix or oklch alpha).

props.name: gridShimmerStroke
props.description: Shimmer band stroke (color and opacity via color-mix or oklch alpha).

props.name: gridShimmer
props.description: Animate a shimmer band across grid lines. Default: true

props.name: gridShimmerLength
props.description: Shimmer band width in pixels. Default: 140

props.name: gridShimmerSpeed
props.description: Shimmer speed multiplier (higher = faster). Default: 1

props.name: gridShimmerSync
props.description: Match shimmer loop to the loading line pulse (cycle + inter-loop pause).

props.name: label
props.description: Centered shimmer label text. Default: "Loading"

props.name: aspectRatio
props.description: Aspect ratio as "width / height". Default: "2 / 1"

props.name: className
props.description: Additional class name for the container

props.name: loopEpoch
props.description: Bumps to restart loop cycles without remounting the stroke.

props.name: strokeOpacity
props.description: Stroke opacity for the animated segment. Default: 0.5

props.name: numTicks
props.description: Explicit tick count (including first and last) — the long-standing override; wins over `tickCount`. Default: unset (→ `tickCount`).

props.name: tickCount
props.description: Tick target (RM-108). `"auto"` (default) derives it from the plot width — `tickTargetForWidth(innerWidth)`, about one tick per 90 px, clamped 2–10, and never more than the number of data rows on a time axis (6 monthly rows get at most 6 ticks, not 9 labels between them).

props.name: ticks
props.description: RM-108 naming, shared with `YAxis`. On a time axis: an alias of `tickValues` (`tickValues` wins). On a numeric x with `domain`/`scale` (ScatterChart): exactly these raw x values.

props.name: domain
props.description: Numeric x only (ScatterChart with numeric `xDataKey`, RM-108): pin either end of the x domain in raw units; `"auto"` keeps the data-derived end. Read by the chart container, so place `XAxis` as a direct child. Setting `domain` or `scale` also switches the labels from one per data row to a numeric ruler. Ignored on a time axis.

props.name: scale
props.description: Numeric x only (RM-108): `"linear"` (default), `"log"` (refuses data or a domain touching 0 — dev warning, renders linear) or `"sqrt"`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which edge the labels sit on (RM-108). Default: `"bottom"`.

props.name: title
props.description: Axis title (RM-108).

props.name: titlePlacement
props.description: `"outside"` (default) — in the margin beyond the tick labels, at the far end; `"inside"` — `HaloText` at the far end inside the plot.

props.name: tickerHalfWidth
props.description: Width of the date ticker box for fade calculation. Default: 50

props.name: tickMode
props.description: `"domain"` — evenly spaced ticks across the time domain (default). `"data"` — one label per data row at its x value (better with sparse or monthly bars).

props.name: tickFormat
props.description: Override the default `Intl`-based tick label formatter. Applied to every tick this axis renders (generated or `tickValues`). #357. **Time scale only.** Ignored (with a dev warning) when the chart runs `xScale="band" | "linear"` — those modes project onto a synthetic instant, so a `Date` formatter would print a fabricated calendar date instead of your x value. Format categorical/numeric x values in your data. #352.

props.name: dateFormat
props.description: The date-format LADDER (RM-109): a preset from `date-format.ts` (`"year"` → `"yearShort"` → `"month"` → `"day"` → `"weekday"` → `"hour"` → `"minute"`), or a formatter function for full control. Unset (default) — the axis picks a rung itself via `dateFormatForSpan`, from the time domain's span and how many ticks are on screen, instead of the old fixed `"Mon d"` shape whatever the span. A ten-year series reads years; a 36-hour series reads hours. `tickFormat` still wins outright when both are set — it is the raw escape hatch this package has always had; `dateFormat` is the smart default underneath it. Same time-scale-only caveat as `tickFormat` (#352).

props.name: tickValues
props.description: Render exactly these tick positions, bypassing tick generation AND the default label-collision de-dupe entirely — use when the default de-dupe would collapse the axis (e.g. dense data whose formatted labels collide). #357. **Time scale only** — see `tickFormat`. #352.

props.name: periodTicks
props.description: Draw a `HairlineFloor` (RM-017) below the plot — one hairline tick per calendar period, whether or not a data row falls on it, with the long tick anchored to a real calendar boundary (day → the first day of the week, week → the first week of the month, month → January), not an index stride from wherever the series happens to start (#253). Lieflat provenance: the ruled foot of a ledger page gives a reader the passage of time with no labels and no axis. This is a SEPARATE visual layer from the labelled ticks above (`numTicks` / `tickMode`) — it never changes which labels render or where. `false` (default) draws nothing — today's behaviour.

props.name: yAxisId
props.description: Scale group id (Recharts `yAxisId`). Default: `"left"`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which side of the chart to render labels. Default: `"left"`.

props.name: numTicks
props.description: Explicit tick count hint for `scale.ticks()` (d3) — the long-standing override; wins over `tickCount`. Actual label count may differ. Clamped to {@link Y_AXIS_MIN_TICK_COUNT}–{@link Y_AXIS_MAX_TICK_COUNT}. Default: unset (→ `tickCount`).

props.name: tickCount
props.description: Tick target (RM-108). `"auto"` (default) derives it from the plot height — `tickTargetForHeight(innerHeight)`: 3 under 200 px, else 5.

props.name: ticks
props.description: Render exactly these tick values (RM-108), bypassing generation.

props.name: domain
props.description: Pin either end of the value domain (RM-108); `"auto"` keeps the data-derived end. Read by the chart container, so place `YAxis` as a direct child. On a length encoding (bars) the domain always includes 0 — a non-zero lower bound is ignored with a dev warning (`charts-honesty`).

props.name: scale
props.description: How values map to pixels (RM-108). `"log"` refuses data or a domain that touches 0 (dev warning, renders linear); bars are linear only. Default: `"linear"`.

props.name: title
props.description: Axis title — names the unit of every tick (RM-108).

props.name: titlePlacement
props.description: `"outside"` (default) — above the top tick label in the margin; `"inside"` — `HaloText` at the top of the axis inside the plot.

props.name: labelPlacement
props.description: `"outside"` (default) — tick labels in the margin beside the plot; `"inside"` — labels sit just above their grid line inside the plot.

props.name: formatLargeNumbers
props.description: @deprecated Superseded by `valueFormat` (see `charts/value-format.ts`), which knows about millions as well as thousands — the old implementation rendered 1 500 000 as `1500k`. `false` still works and is equivalent to `valueFormat="number"`; `true` is now the default behaviour and can be dropped. Removed in the next major (`docs/DEPRECATION.md` §1).

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: How tick values are rendered. Default: `"compact"` — `1.5M`, not `1500k` and not `1500000`. Pass `"number"` for every digit.

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO 4217 code for `valueFormat: "currency"`. Falls back to `ChartConfigProvider`, then `"USD"`.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Custom formatter for tick labels. Overrides `valueFormat` entirely when set.

props.name: unit
props.description: Unit text appended to {@link unitOn} tick(s) — `<YAxis unit="%" />` paints `"80 %"` on that tick, not every tick (RM-109). The tooltip is the place a unit repeats on every value (the blog's "3.4 % unemployed", not a bare "3.4 %"); see `TooltipRow.unit`.

props.name: unitOn
props.description: Which tick(s) {@link unit} paints on. Default: `"last"`.

stories.name: With Reference Line
stories.description: A labelled threshold on the series’ own y-scale — a target, a budget, an SLA. Drawn in `--chart-foreground` with a dash (meaning, not gridline) and a haloed label; it stays outside the reveal clip like `Grid`.

stories.name: Drilldown
stories.description: Click anywhere on the plot — or Tab in and press Enter — to drill in.

stories.name: Density comparison
stories.description: #394: the axis tick label reads the `text-meta` ROLE (was the raw `text‑xs` utility, which `data-density`/#340 cannot reach). Two columns pin `data-density` on a plain wrapping div — NOT `<ThemeProvider>`, which writes `data-density` to `document.documentElement` and would race two columns — mirroring `Foundations/Typography → Density scale`'s pattern. The measured font-size is read live from the browser so the columns cannot claim a scaling they do not render. Must match `Gantt`'s already-density-aware timescale tick (11.25px compact / 12px comfortable / 12.75px spacious, styling-and-tokens.md).

stories.name: Weekend Hollow
stories.description: `markerStyle` (RM-028): a hollow dot means weekend, a filled dot means weekday — the lieflat "hairline line, weekend/weekday marker" idiom. Every point still gets a marker; only the fill/stroke resolution differs.

stories.name: Top Three Peaks
stories.description: `labelPeaks` (RM-028): the top-k highest points get an enlarged marker and a `HaloText` value label — lieflat's "top-2/top-3 peaks, enlarged and labelled" rule. This series has exactly three well-separated spikes, so all three are labelled.

stories.name: Barcode Floor
stories.description: `periodTicks="day"` (RM-028): a `HairlineFloor` tick for every calendar day — 90 of them — whether or not a label renders there, with the long tick anchored to the first day of the week (Monday), not an index stride from the series' start date (#253). The labelled ticks above are a SEPARATE layer — `ninetyDaySeries` starts 2024-01-01, so they land at an even 22-day stride (`Jan 1, Jan 23, Feb 14, Mar 7, Mar 30`), not month boundaries; `periodTicks` never changes that. Acceptance: 90 ticks, every 7th long (a weekly boundary), the long tick painted in its own higher- contrast ink, and no collision between the labelled ticks at 400px width.

stories.name: Nulls — gap
stories.description: `nulls="gap"` (the default) breaks the line at a non-numeric sample — a visible hole, never a silent zero or a straight bridge over missing data.

stories.name: Nulls — connect
stories.description: `nulls="connect"` draws one continuous line straight across the missing sample.

stories.name: Nulls — zero
stories.description: `nulls="zero"` — the pre-RM-112 default — reads a missing sample as 0.

stories.name: Curve comparison
stories.description: `curve` (RM-112) — a named alias over `@visx/curve`. The default changed from `"natural"` to `"monotone"`: `curveNatural` can overshoot past a flat plateau's own value (visible on the middle two, equal-height points below), which reads as a false peak; `curveMonotoneX` is built to never do that. `"step-after"` is shown as a third, structurally distinct alias.

stories.name: Outline
stories.description: `outline` (RM-112) paints a `--chart-background` halo under the coloured stroke, so a line keeps reading as one continuous path through a crossing with another series or a busy grid — Datawrapper's line-outline idiom.

stories.name: Symbols
stories.description: `symbols` (RM-112) — Datawrapper's line-symbols vocabulary. Unset placement on a ≤12-point series defaults to hollow markers at the first/last point only; a dense series (>12 points) stays unmarked unless `placement` is set explicitly. Same resolution rule, one shared helper, on `Area` too.

stories.name: Focus on hover
stories.description: `focusOnHover` (RM-112) dims every OTHER series to `SELECTION_EXCLUDED_OPACITY` while the pointer (or the legend) is over one — a spotlight for a busy multi-series chart. A wide, invisible hit-stroke keeps the hover target reliable even at the default, thin 2.5px stroke.

stories.name: Selection states
stories.description: `selectionStates` paints the host’s tri-state on each category’s points: selected marks carry a compound foreground/background outline, excluded marks dim AND carry a full-opacity dashed frame, so the three states stay distinguishable in greyscale.

stories.name: Legend from column keys
stories.description: Built by hand from the SAME normalized series `AutoChart`'s `LineLegendFromColumnKeys` story forwards (`spec.series: [{ key: "ebikes" }, { key: "cargo" }]`, no `name` — the legend engine always labels an item by its `dataKey`, never a display `name`). Its `.legend-container` is byte-identical to that story's — proof that `AutoChart` forwards into `LineChart`'s own `legend` prop rather than running a second implementation (Acceptance-4).

stories.name: Legend at xs and sm density
stories.description: Density tiers the container legend engine (RM-118) reads from `ChartConfigProvider` (RM-072, a host-picked furniture tier — never derived from viewport width): `xs` has no room at all, so an explicitly-on legend renders nothing; `sm` keeps the legend but always stacks it (one item per line), the same as a `narrow` breakpoint.

stories.name: Legend suppresses the redundant key row
stories.description: R4 (sitting 3, RM-118): two long series names overflow RM-110's own end labels at a narrow width, which normally falls back to `SeriesKeyRow` — a compact swatch+name row inside the plot. But `legend` is also forced on here, and the container legend (unlike the pre-RM-118 inline `<ChartLegend>` child) STAYS visible and stacked at narrow by design (Acceptance bullet 1). Rendering both would show the same series list twice, so `legendVisible` (`time-series-chart-shell.tsx`) suppresses the key row whenever the container legend already covers that job — the plot itself never reserves less space, only the redundant row disappears.

dataShapes: a metric updating in real time, appended over a rolling window
intent.avoidWhen: the series is static or historical — use a line chart

charts/metricgrid.name: MetricGrid
charts/metricgrid.title: Charts/MetricGrid
charts/metricgrid.summary: Responsive grid of KPI tiles — the summary row at the top of a dashboard.

intent.purpose: Responsive grid of KPI tiles — the summary row at the top of a dashboard.
antiPatterns: More than ~5 tiles in one row — KPIs answer 'how are we doing', not 'everything we measure'.
Numbers without tabular-nums — figures jitter across the row.
Re-declaring a KPI tile locally — MetricCard is owned by @elabs-ai/components-ui and re-exported here (ADR 0012).

props.name: children
props.description: Optional so a `loading` grid can render its placeholder shape before any tiles exist.

props.name: columns
props.description: Target columns at the largest breakpoint. Defaults to 4.

props.name: reveal
props.description: Stagger the tiles in on mount. Motion-gated. Defaults to false (dashboards opt in).

props.name: featured
props.description: Index of the tile that spans wider (research 11 §B.5 KPI-2) — pairs with `<MetricCard emphasis="headline">` so the headline KPI out-ranks the band.

props.name: featuredSpan
props.description: Columns the featured tile spans at the larger breakpoints. Defaults to 2.

props.name: loading
props.description: Loading vs ready — forwards `loading` to every child tile; when there are no children yet, renders `columns` placeholder `MetricCard`s so the grid reserves its final shape. Default: `false`.

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: How to render a NUMERIC `value`. Default: `"compact"`. Ignored for every other `ReactNode` — a string you already formatted is rendered verbatim.

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO 4217 code for `valueFormat: "currency"`. Default: `"USD"`.

props.name: copyExactValue
props.description: Offer the exact figure on click when a numeric `value` was shortened. Default: `true`. Turning it off leaves a compacted number with no way back to its digits, so only do that when the tile is decorative.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary line under the value — sublabel / context.

props.name: delta
props.description: Signed change, e.g. "+12.4%". Direction colors it.

props.name: positiveIsGood
props.description: Whether "up" is good (green) — flip for metrics where down is good.

props.name: visual
props.description: Optional inline visual shown under the value/description.

props.name: sparkline

props.name: evidence
props.description: Optional grounding footer (research 11 §B.5 KPI-3) — connects a cited figure to its source (e.g. an `EvidenceChip` from `@elabs-ai/components-ai`). Rendered subdued (`text-meta text-muted-foreground`) under the tile body.

props.name: loading
props.description: Loading vs ready — renders a layout-shaped skeleton (matching the real box height) instead of the value/label/delta text. Default: `false`.

props.name: announceLoading
props.description: Whether this tile announces its own `loading` state via a live region. Set to `false` when several tiles are composed inside a container that already announces once for the whole region (e.g. a loading `MetricGrid`) — see loading-states.md §a11y ("one live region per region, not per box"). Default: `true`.

stories.name: Loading
stories.description: Loading vs ready (#268) — `loading` forwards to every tile, matching each card's box height.

stories.name: Loading Empty
stories.description: Loading with no children yet — reserves the grid's final shape with placeholder tiles.

charts/networkchart.name: NetworkChart
charts/networkchart.title: Charts/NetworkChart
charts/networkchart.summary: A node-link graph in three layouts — a settled force cloud, a ring of chords, or a bipartite colonnade — with hover/focus adjacency emphasis.

intent.purpose: A node-link graph in three layouts — a settled force cloud, a ring of chords, or a bipartite colonnade — with hover/focus adjacency emphasis.

stateTokens.node: --chart-1 … --chart-12 by group via resolvePalette (categorical at or under 6 groups, mono above); the mark is stroked in the paper colour (--chart-background) so touching nodes still read apart
stateTokens.link: --chart-grid hairlines at 0.35 opacity, width scaled by the link's own value
stateTokens.emphasis: hover/focus dims non-neighbours to opacity 0.12 and non-incident links to 0.03 — a CLASS on each <g>, transitioned on the compositor, so no node re-renders per frame
stateTokens.label: HaloText in the chart-source type role, punched from var(--chart-background); drawn only at or above labelThreshold
stateTokens.focus: every node is a real button in ChartDatapointLayer beside the aria-hidden SVG (never inside it), carrying the shared compound focus indicator (--ring plus the --ring-contour outline), shown only on keyboard focus; one tab stop, arrows across the rest

antiPatterns: Reading a force layout's POSITIONS as data — only adjacency is encoded; distance, direction and the picture's orientation are artefacts of the solver's seed. Use layout="circular" or "arc" whenever position must mean something.

Labelling every node past roughly 15 — set `labelThreshold` so only the nodes worth naming carry text; an unreadable label ring is noise, and the datapoint targets already announce every node to a screen reader.

Reaching for layout="arc" on a graph that is not bipartite — the two columns are DERIVED (exactly two groups, else the nodes that are only ever a link source go left), so a general graph draws a colonnade that asserts a split the data does not have.

Turning `draggable` on and expecting the dragged position to persist — a node springs back on release because the settled layout is the answer; a pinned position would be a claim about the data that the layout never made.

Passing thousands of nodes because `maxNodes` is only a warning — the force solve is synchronous, so past a few hundred nodes it blocks the frame that renders it. Aggregate into hubs before the chart, not inside it.
dataShapes: arbitrary node and edge relationships with no hierarchy
intent.avoidWhen: the relationship really is a hierarchy — use a tree chart or a treemap

props.name: nodes
props.description: The graph's nodes. `id` is the identity `links` reference.

props.name: links
props.description: The graph's edges. An endpoint naming an unknown node is dropped (dev warning).

props.name: layout
props.description: - `"force"` — a settled force-directed cloud (G11, B2). - `"circular"` — one ring, chords bundled toward the centre (G6, B1). - `"arc"` — bipartite ownership: two columns, hairline béziers (L12).

props.name: nodeSize
props.description: `"value"` (default) — AREA is proportional to the node's weight, i.e. radius ∝ √weight. A number pins every node to that radius. "Weight" is the node's own `value`, or its DEGREE when it has none — which is what gives a colonnade "hub radius ∝ link count" for free.

props.name: labelThreshold
props.description: Draw a node's label only when its weight reaches this (lieflat B1's rule for a 60-node ring). Omit to label every node — right for ≤ ~15 nodes, unreadable above it.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: `"adjacency"` (default) — hovering or focusing a node keeps it and its neighbours lit and blurs the rest. `"none"` disables it.

props.name: draggable
props.description: `force` only: let the pointer pull a node out of place. It springs back to its settled position on release — the layout is the answer, the drag is a way to look under a cluster. Ignored (with a dev warning) on the other two layouts, which have no free positions to give.

props.name: palette
props.description: Colour family. Default: `"categorical"` at or under six groups, `"mono"` above — past six, a hue per group names nothing.

props.name: maxNodes
props.description: Dev-warning threshold on node count. Default 200. NOT a cap.

props.name: seed
props.description: `force` only: changes the starting cloud, and so which arrangement is found.

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: How node values render in the tooltip. Default `"compact"`.

props.name: aspectRatio
props.description: Aspect ratio as "width / height". Default `"16 / 9"`.

props.name: plotHeight
props.description: The plot's own height (ADR 0039): px, or `{ aspect }` (width ÷ height), optionally per breakpoint. Wins over `aspectRatio`, which stays an alias.

props.name: accessibleLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the chart region. Defaults to the auto summary — `"Network, 60 nodes, 140 links, 5 groups"` — because the counts are exactly what an `aria-hidden` SVG withholds.

props.name: accessibleDescription
props.description: Supplemental description read by AT.

stories.name: Small Circular
stories.description: **G6 — the small ring.** Twelve nodes, every one labelled, chords bundled toward the centre so a dense middle still reads. The ring is the right answer under ~15 nodes: position carries no meaning, so nothing is lost by fixing it, and the eye gets a stable place to look each node up.

stories.name: Small Force
stories.description: **G11 — the small force cloud.** The same graph, laid out by attraction and repulsion instead of by decree: clusters that talk to each other end up together, and the Data tier falls out on its own. The simulation does NOT tick. It is solved to a fixed 300-tick budget from a seeded start before React sees a coordinate, so the picture is identical on every render, in every process — and nothing moves under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

stories.name: Big Circular
stories.description: **B1 — the big ring.** Sixty nodes is past the point where every label fits, so `labelThreshold` names only the people worth naming; the rest stay dots. Hover or focus any node: it and its neighbours stay lit and everything else blurs, which is the only way a 140-chord ring answers "who does this one work with". The blur is a CSS class on each `<g>`, driven by ONE piece of state — no node re-renders on hover, which is what keeps it at 60 fps here and at 180 nodes.

stories.name: Big Force
stories.description: **B2 — the big force cloud.** 180 nodes, hubs and satellites. The whole layout is solved synchronously in well under the 500 ms budget, and it is the SAME layout every time.

stories.name: Ownership
stories.description: **L12 — the ownership colonnade.** Two columns, hairline béziers, and no node `value` at all: with nothing to size by, a node's radius follows its DEGREE, so a team that owns five services reads as a hub without anyone computing a number for it. The split is derived, not declared — exactly two groups puts one on each side; failing that, the nodes that are only ever a link's `source` go left.

stories.name: Draggable
stories.description: **Drag (force only).** Pull a node aside to look under a cluster; it springs back to its settled position on release, because the settled layout IS the answer and a dragged position would be a lie about the data. Dragging is a pointer affordance. The keyboard path sits beside it: one tab stop into the chart, arrows across every node, each target named with its degree. That path is mounted by `onDatapointClick` (or `copyValueOnActivate`), not by `draggable` — so this story sets a handler, and its play function proves the path is really there (#274).

stories.name: Keyboard Drilldown
stories.description: Every node is a keyboard datapoint target — a real `<button>` in a `pointer-events: none` layer BESIDE the `aria-hidden` SVG, never inside it. The target's own accessible name carries the node's degree, so the answer a sighted user reads in the tooltip reaches a screen-reader user too.

charts/parallelcoordinateschart.name: ParallelCoordinatesChart
charts/parallelcoordinateschart.title: Charts/ParallelCoordinatesChart
charts/parallelcoordinateschart.summary: Same entities across 3-6 mixed-unit dimensions: one hairline per entity threaded through per-axis-normalized vertical scales, so shape and crossing pattern reveal correlation across axes that share no common unit.

intent.purpose: Same entities across 3-6 mixed-unit dimensions: one hairline per entity threaded through per-axis-normalized vertical scales, so shape and crossing pattern reveal correlation across axes that share no common unit.

stateTokens.axis: var(--chart-foreground-muted) vertical hairline with end ticks (HairlineFloor style)
stateTokens.extremeLabel: var(--chart-foreground-muted) on a var(--chart-background) halo, axis feet only when showExtremes
stateTokens.heroLine: 2px, var(--chart-foreground) or the resolved palette ink, opacity 1 — drawn LAST so it sits on top
stateTokens.nonHeroLine: 0.65px hairline, seeded 0.5-0.8 opacity — a texture of many lines, not individually legible

antiPatterns: Fewer than 3 or more than 6 dimensions — below 3 a DumbbellChart (2) or MetricCard (1) reads better; above 6 the axes crowd and `resolveParallelDimensions` clamps to the first 6 with a console warning, silently dropping the rest.

Dimensions on wildly different natural scales with no explicit `domain` — each axis normalizes independently, so an unset domain just uses that dimension's own min/max, which is usually right; only override when you need a domain that isn't in the data (e.g. a known 0-100 ceiling).

Using `highlightKey` to try to promote MULTIPLE entities to hero status — only the first row a predicate matches (or the one literal id) is promoted; for comparing several entities at once, dim the rest via a different technique or fall back to small multiples.

Reaching for this when the entities do NOT share the same dimensions, or when there is only one entity — a single-entity profile across many metrics is a RadarChart (shared 0-100 radial scale) or a MetricGrid, not a parallel-coordinates plot.
dataShapes: many numeric dimensions compared across entities at once
intent.avoidWhen: more than about 2 entities need per-entity detail — use small-multiple radar

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the target group. Defaults to a localized generic name.

stories.name: Default
stories.description: Twelve products across four mixed-unit dimensions — the L20 acceptance recreation. No hero: every hairline draws at its seeded 0.5–0.8 opacity.

stories.name: Hero Line
stories.description: `highlightKey` as a literal entity id promotes ONE line to the 2px hero — drawn last (on top) with a halo label at its final axis point.

stories.name: Hero By Predicate
stories.description: `highlightKey` as a predicate promotes the first row it matches — here, the first product clearing an NPS of 50.

stories.name: Show Extremes
stories.description: `showExtremes` draws each axis's min/max value at its foot.

stories.name: Monotone Curve
stories.description: `curve="monotone"` draws a smoothed `curveMonotoneX` bézier between axes instead of a straight hairline segment.

stories.name: Categorical Few Entities
stories.description: Three axes (the minimum) with an explicit `categorical` palette, honoured up to the six-entity soft cap.

stories.name: Keyboard Cycling
stories.description: Setting `onDatapointClick` mounts the keyboard/pointer interaction layer — arrow keys cycle through every entity, Enter activates. Verifies the roadmap's "keyboard cycles through entities" acceptance bullet.

charts/piechart.name: PieChart
charts/piechart.title: Charts/PieChart
charts/piechart.summary: Part-of-whole split across a handful of categories.

intent.purpose: Part-of-whole split across a handful of categories.
antiPatterns: More than ~5 slices — a bar chart compares better; a pie is not a ranking.
A pie for values that don't sum to a meaningful whole.
Identifying slices by color alone — put the label and value on or beside the slice.
dataShapes: parts of a whole across a few categories, read as proportions of the total
intent.avoidWhen: more than about 6 slices — use a bar or unit chart

props.name: data
props.description: Data array - each item represents a slice

props.name: size
props.description: Chart size in pixels. If not provided, uses parent container size

props.name: plotHeight
props.description: The plot's own height (ADR 0039): px, or `{ aspect }` (width ÷ height), optionally per breakpoint.

props.name: innerRadius
props.description: Inner radius for donut charts, in px — or, below `1`, as a fraction of the outer radius (`0.6` keeps a responsive donut a donut at every size). Default: 0 (solid pie)

props.name: align
props.description: Where the square plot sits in a container wider than it is tall: `"start"` (default, as before) or `"center"` — centred, and outside labels may run past the square into the free room either side instead of being clipped at it.

props.name: padAngle
props.description: Padding angle between slices in radians. Default: 0

props.name: cornerRadius
props.description: Corner radius for rounded slice edges. Default: 0

props.name: startAngle
props.description: Start angle in radians. Default: -PI/2 (top)

props.name: endAngle
props.description: End angle in radians. Default: 3*PI/2 (full circle from top)

props.name: className
props.description: Additional class name for the container

props.name: hoveredIndex
props.description: Controlled hover state - index of hovered slice

props.name: onHoverChange
props.description: Callback when hover state changes

props.name: hoverOffset
props.description: Hover offset in pixels for slice hover effects. This also determines the padding around the chart to prevent clipping. Default: 10

props.name: children
props.description: Child components (PieSlice, PieCenter, patterns, gradients, etc.)

props.name: onDatapointClick
props.description: Drill-down (#349). Fires when a slice is activated by pointer OR keyboard. Setting it mounts a keyboard-operable target layer OUTSIDE the aria-hidden SVG — one tab stop, arrow keys to traverse. Unset changes nothing.

props.name: copyValueOnActivate
props.description: Put the datapoint's exact value on the clipboard when it is activated — the recovery path for a compact axis label. Default `false`; a chart with no interaction props still renders byte-identical DOM. A consumer-supplied `onDatapointClick` always wins.

props.name: datapointLabel
props.description: Override the accessible name of each keyboard drill-down target (#349).

props.name: maxInteractiveDatapoints
props.description: Dev-warning threshold on the number of keyboard targets. Default 500 (#349).

props.name: accessibleLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the chart region (announces to AT on focus).

props.name: accessibleDescription
props.description: Supplemental description read by AT (e.g. slice names + value range).

props.name: enterTransition
props.description: Framer Motion transition for slice enter animation

props.name: enterStaggerScale
props.description: Scales slice stagger delays (1 = default).

props.name: geometryScrubbing
props.description: High-frequency geometry updates (e.g. studio NumberField scrub). Uses plain SVG paths instead of Motion `d` / spring hover morphing.

props.name: radiusKey
props.description: Second measure driving each slice's OUTER radius — angle × radius double encoding (lieflat G13 "Big Slice", #RM-030). Reads `data[i][radiusKey]` as a number; `outerRadius = innerRadius + (R - innerRadius) * sqrt(v / max)` (area-honest — equal AREA differences read as equal magnitude differences, not equal radius differences). A slice whose value is missing/non-numeric — or every slice, when `radiusKey` is unset — renders at the chart's full outer radius, today's behavior.

props.name: referenceRings
props.description: Dashed reference rings (in `radiusKey`'s units) with small value labels — e.g. `[15, 30, 45]` for a "minutes/day" second measure. No-op when `radiusKey` is unset.

props.name: seams
props.description: Paper-seam stroke (px) drawn between slices — the lieflat "3px paper seam" cut-paper look. Default: `0` (no seam — today's behavior).

props.name: labels
props.description: Slice labels (RM-114, Datawrapper parity) — inside/outside placement, `label`/`value`/`percent` facts, leaders on the outside ring. Unset renders nothing extra (today's behavior).

props.name: legend
props.description: Container legend (RM-118): one swatch per slice, mounted outside the plot via `useContainerLegend`. Unset renders nothing (R1) — today's behavior. Pie has no competing on-chart key the way `colorBy` (Bar) or RM-115's colour/shape key (Scatter) do, so R4's "one key per chart" never applies here. Hover-only (R3): hovering or focusing a legend item reuses Pie's own existing single-slice hover state — the SAME one a pointer hovering a slice already writes into (`hoveredIndex`/`onHoverChange` above) — so a legend hover and a pointer hover dim every other slice identically. An `interactive: "toggle"` request downgrades to `"hover"`: Pie has no hide-a-slice wiring yet (a hidden slice would silently change every other slice's percentage, which needs its own design pass — tracked as a follow-up, not built here).

props.name: groupSmall
props.description: Fold the smallest slices into one trailing "Other" slice (RM-114, `pie-grouping.ts`). **Setting this hands slice rendering to `PieChart` itself** — any `PieSlice` elements in `children` are ignored (their indices would no longer match the folded result); keep `PieCenter` and defs/gradient children, they are unaffected. Unset: today's behavior, `children` renders verbatim.

props.name: sort
props.description: Wedge order. `"desc"` — `startAngle` gets the LARGEST slice, then clockwise by descending size (d3-shape's own pie default). `"none"` (the default here) keeps `data`'s own order — pre-RM-114 behavior, kept as the default so an existing chart's wedge ANGLES never move under it (see the docblock on `effectiveSort` in `PieChartBase` for why the RM's stated `"desc"` default was not adopted). Slice INDEX identity never changes either way — a `<PieSlice index={i}>` always targets `data[i]`; only the angular position can move.

props.name: half
props.description: The "election donut" preset (RM-114): `startAngle: -π/2, endAngle: π/2` — a dome across the top half, seated in data order by default (`sort` unset here behaves exactly as elsewhere: `"none"`). The centre slot (a `PieCenter` child) is positioned BELOW the arc instead of in the chart's geometric middle. Overrides any `startAngle`/`endAngle` props. Default `false`.

charts/inview.name: InView
charts/inview.title: Charts/Reveal/InView
charts/inview.about: RM-020 — `revealOn="inView"` + `replayOnClick` on `ChartRevealClip`. These demos exercise the RM-020 primitive DIRECTLY, via a minimal chart-shaped harness rather than a real `LineChart`/`AreaChart`/`BarChart` — kept that way so this story's geometry (viewport height, spacer height, `amount: 0.3` threshold) stays exactly reasoned-about and the play function's assertions stay about the PRIMITIVE, not about a real chart's own rendered height. `LineChart`, `AreaChart` and `BarChart` expose `revealOn`/ `replayOnClick` on their public props since #175, all reading the same gate (`useChartRevealGate`); `BarChart`'s real-chart demos are `Charts/BarChart` → `RevealInView` / `ReplayOnClick`.

stories.name: In View
stories.description: Three stacked charts, each ~700px below the fold except the first. Only the chart that has actually scrolled into view (30% visible) plays its enter reveal — `chart-reveal-clip.test.tsx` covers the gating decision itself with a fake `IntersectionObserver`; this story is the real-browser proof that scrolling a genuine `IntersectionObserver` triggers it.

stories.name: Replay On Click
stories.description: The replay affordance, both halves — the reference wiring for `replayOnClick`. - **Pointer:** clicking the chart body replays the reveal; clicking the "bar" datapoint fires its own handler and does NOT replay (`shouldReplayOnClick`). - **Keyboard (#176):** a real `<button>` rendered OUTSIDE the chart body bumps `replayCount`, which goes through the same replay epoch as a click. Tab to it, press Enter or Space, and the reveal replays. `replayOnClick` alone is a mouse-only enhancement — a listener on an element chosen for intersection observation has no role, no name and no tab stop — so never ship it without a control like this one.
