charts/scatterchart.name: ScatterChart
charts/scatterchart.title: Charts/ScatterChart
charts/scatterchart.summary: Point cloud for correlation between two continuous measures.

intent.purpose: Point cloud for correlation between two continuous measures.
antiPatterns: Connecting the points — a line asserts a sequence a scatter does not have.
Plotting tens of thousands of raw points — bin or sample; the browser and the reader both give up.
Distinguishing groups by colour only at default opacity — overlapping marks collapse; add shape or facets.
dataShapes: two continuous measures per row — correlation, or the shape of a distribution
intent.avoidWhen: one axis is categorical — use a bar or dumbbell chart

props.name: data
props.description: Data array — each item should have a date field and numeric values

props.name: xDataKey
props.description: Key in data for the x-axis (date). Default: "date"

props.name: xScale
props.description: How `xDataKey` values are interpreted (#302). Default: `"time"`, unless every value is already a `number`, which infers `"linear"` — a numeric x (weight, price, …) then renders numeric tick labels and a numeric tooltip title instead of an epoch date. A categorical x remains unsupported (still warns); only `"time"`/`"linear"` are offered.

props.name: margin
props.description: Chart margins

props.name: animationDuration
props.description: Animation duration in milliseconds. Default: 1100

props.name: animationEasing
props.description: CSS easing for clip-reveal. Default: cubic-bezier(0.85, 0, 0.15, 1)

props.name: aspectRatio
props.description: Aspect ratio as "width / height". Default: "2 / 1"

props.name: plotHeight
props.description: The plot's own height (ADR 0039): px, or `{ aspect }` (width ÷ height), optionally per breakpoint. Wins over `aspectRatio`, which stays an alias.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional class name for the container

props.name: children
props.description: Child components (Scatter, Grid, ChartTooltip, XAxis, etc.)

props.name: accessibleLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the chart region (announces to AT on focus).

props.name: accessibleDescription
props.description: Supplemental description read by AT (e.g. series names + value range).

props.name: legend
props.description: Renders a legend beside the plot via `useContainerLegend` (RM-118). Unset renders nothing (R1). `true` uses the default placement/layout; `{ position, layout, values, title }` refines it — `interactive` is capped at `"hover"` (a legend row highlights on hover/focus but never toggles a series' visibility — Scatter has no per-series hide, unlike `BarChart`). One key per chart (RM-118 R4): when any `<Scatter colorBy>` child resolves a non-empty colour key (`resolveColorBy`, `scatter-encodings.ts` — the same categorical/sequential/diverging stops the points themselves draw), the legend lists THAT key instead of the plain per-series (`dataKey`) rows, so only one key ever shows. `shapeBy`'s categories are not represented here — the legend engine has no shape-swatch marker yet (`ChartLegendEntry.marker` doesn't cover it); a `shapeBy`-only chart keeps the plain per-series legend.

props.name: yAxisId
props.description: Y-scale group id (Recharts `yAxisId`). Default: `"left"`.

props.name: animate
props.description: Whether to animate points with clip reveal. Default: true

props.name: yGradient
props.description: Color each dot by its vertical position using a chart-space linear gradient. Lower values use `from`; higher values use `to`. Default stops: red (bottom) → green (top).

props.name: dropLines
props.description: Draw a hairline "drop line" from each point down to the axis it names — `"x"` to the bottom (x) axis, `"y"` to the left (y) axis, `"both"` for both. Rendered UNDER the markers and excluded from hit-testing (`pointer-events: none`, `aria-hidden`). Default: `false` — no drop lines, today's behavior.

props.name: labelExtremes
props.type: { /** Rank by the series' own value (`"y"`) or by x-axis position (`"x"`). */ by: "y" | "x"; /** How many points to label at EACH end (best and worst). Default: 1. */ count?: number; /** Data field to read the point's display label from. */ labelKey?: string; /** Formats the ranked numeric value next to the label. */ format?: (value: number) => string; }
props.description: Hero-and-rest labeling (lieflat F8 "Plumb Scatter"): mark the `count` highest AND `count` lowest points (ranked `by`) in full-opacity ink with a `HaloText` label, fading every other point to `fadedOpacity`. `labelKey` names the data field to read the display label from; when omitted the label falls back to the chart's own x-axis date label for that row. `format`, when given, formats the numeric value alongside the label (only applied when the ranked value is a number, i.e. `by: "y"`).

props.name: fadedOpacity
props.description: Opacity applied to points NOT selected by `labelExtremes`. Default: 0.35.

props.name: jitter
props.description: Deterministic jitter (`seededRnd` — identical across re-renders and test runs), as a fraction of the row band, `0–0.5`. Requires `yType="category"`; ignored otherwise.

props.name: yType
props.description: Treat this series' values (`d[dataKey]`) as category labels laid out on a local band scale (one row per distinct value) rather than a numeric y position on the chart's shared y-scale. Default: `"number"` — today's behavior.

props.name: highlightKey
props.description: Highlight matching points with a non-color ring (`PeakRing` — shape, not hue, carries the emphasis; see `.claude/rules/accessibility.md`). A string names a data field read as a truthy flag (`d[highlightKey]`); a function is called with the row and returns whether it is highlighted.

props.name: sizeKey
props.description: Bubble size by a numeric column (RM-115) — `d[sizeKey]` scales the marker's radius by `sqrt(value / max)` (honesty gate: AREA, not radius, carries the value — see `areaRadius`). Rows missing `sizeKey` (or the whole series, when `sizeKey` is set but every value is non-numeric) draw at `sizeRange[0]`. Unset (default): every marker draws at `radius`.

props.name: sizeRange
props.description: `[minRadius, maxRadius]` in px for `sizeKey`. Default: `[4, 22]`.

props.name: colorBy
props.description: Colour each point by a fixed/categorical/numeric column (RM-115) instead of the series' own colour. A row whose `colorBy.key` is missing/unusable keeps drawing in the series' own `fill`. See `scatter-encodings.ts`' `resolveColorBy` — a consumer building a legend (RM-118) calls it with the same `data`/`colorBy` to get the identical colour stops.

props.name: shapeBy
props.description: Shape each point by a categorical column (RM-115), cycling through the series-marker ramp (≤ 6 shapes; a 7th+ distinct value repeats the last shape). See `resolveShapeBy` for the legend a consumer (RM-118) reads.

props.name: trend
props.description: A least-squares trend line (RM-115): `"linear"` (`y = a + bx`) or `"log"` (`y = a + b·ln(x)`, points with a non-positive x dropped). `false` (default): no trend line. See `trend-line.tsx` for the regression space it fits in and its accuracy caveat for `"log"` on a `xScale="linear"` chart.

props.name: labels
props.description: Point labels with collision avoidance (RM-110): `{ key, mode?, priority? }` — `key` is the row field holding the label text; `mode` `"auto"` (default: thinned by plot area, fewer at narrow widths) | `"all"` | a predicate; `priority` decides who survives (default: the y value). Wave-1 integration (RM-115 × RM-110): when `sizeKey` is set and `labels` does not supply its own `priority`, the bubble's OWN `sizeKey` value becomes the priority reader — the biggest bubbles keep their labels first, matching what the eye already reads as "important" on a bubble chart. Every label that is not painted is restated `sr-only` by the chart. Unlike `labelExtremes` it never fades the unlabelled points.

props.name: numTicks
props.description: Explicit tick count (including first and last) — the long-standing override; wins over `tickCount`. Default: unset (→ `tickCount`).

props.name: tickCount
props.description: Tick target (RM-108). `"auto"` (default) derives it from the plot width — `tickTargetForWidth(innerWidth)`, about one tick per 90 px, clamped 2–10, and never more than the number of data rows on a time axis (6 monthly rows get at most 6 ticks, not 9 labels between them).

props.name: ticks
props.description: RM-108 naming, shared with `YAxis`. On a time axis: an alias of `tickValues` (`tickValues` wins). On a numeric x with `domain`/`scale` (ScatterChart): exactly these raw x values.

props.name: domain
props.description: Numeric x only (ScatterChart with numeric `xDataKey`, RM-108): pin either end of the x domain in raw units; `"auto"` keeps the data-derived end. Read by the chart container, so place `XAxis` as a direct child. Setting `domain` or `scale` also switches the labels from one per data row to a numeric ruler. Ignored on a time axis.

props.name: scale
props.description: Numeric x only (RM-108): `"linear"` (default), `"log"` (refuses data or a domain touching 0 — dev warning, renders linear) or `"sqrt"`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which edge the labels sit on (RM-108). Default: `"bottom"`.

props.name: title
props.description: Axis title (RM-108).

props.name: titlePlacement
props.description: `"outside"` (default) — in the margin beyond the tick labels, at the far end; `"inside"` — `HaloText` at the far end inside the plot.

props.name: tickerHalfWidth
props.description: Width of the date ticker box for fade calculation. Default: 50

props.name: tickMode
props.description: `"domain"` — evenly spaced ticks across the time domain (default). `"data"` — one label per data row at its x value (better with sparse or monthly bars).

props.name: tickFormat
props.description: Override the default `Intl`-based tick label formatter. Applied to every tick this axis renders (generated or `tickValues`). #357. **Time scale only.** Ignored (with a dev warning) when the chart runs `xScale="band" | "linear"` — those modes project onto a synthetic instant, so a `Date` formatter would print a fabricated calendar date instead of your x value. Format categorical/numeric x values in your data. #352.

props.name: dateFormat
props.description: The date-format LADDER (RM-109): a preset from `date-format.ts` (`"year"` → `"yearShort"` → `"month"` → `"day"` → `"weekday"` → `"hour"` → `"minute"`), or a formatter function for full control. Unset (default) — the axis picks a rung itself via `dateFormatForSpan`, from the time domain's span and how many ticks are on screen, instead of the old fixed `"Mon d"` shape whatever the span. A ten-year series reads years; a 36-hour series reads hours. `tickFormat` still wins outright when both are set — it is the raw escape hatch this package has always had; `dateFormat` is the smart default underneath it. Same time-scale-only caveat as `tickFormat` (#352).

props.name: tickValues
props.description: Render exactly these tick positions, bypassing tick generation AND the default label-collision de-dupe entirely — use when the default de-dupe would collapse the axis (e.g. dense data whose formatted labels collide). #357. **Time scale only** — see `tickFormat`. #352.

props.name: periodTicks
props.description: Draw a `HairlineFloor` (RM-017) below the plot — one hairline tick per calendar period, whether or not a data row falls on it, with the long tick anchored to a real calendar boundary (day → the first day of the week, week → the first week of the month, month → January), not an index stride from wherever the series happens to start (#253). Lieflat provenance: the ruled foot of a ledger page gives a reader the passage of time with no labels and no axis. This is a SEPARATE visual layer from the labelled ticks above (`numTicks` / `tickMode`) — it never changes which labels render or where. `false` (default) draws nothing — today's behaviour.

props.name: yAxisId
props.description: Scale group id (Recharts `yAxisId`). Default: `"left"`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which side of the chart to render labels. Default: `"left"`.

props.name: numTicks
props.description: Explicit tick count hint for `scale.ticks()` (d3) — the long-standing override; wins over `tickCount`. Actual label count may differ. Clamped to {@link Y_AXIS_MIN_TICK_COUNT}–{@link Y_AXIS_MAX_TICK_COUNT}. Default: unset (→ `tickCount`).

props.name: tickCount
props.description: Tick target (RM-108). `"auto"` (default) derives it from the plot height — `tickTargetForHeight(innerHeight)`: 3 under 200 px, else 5.

props.name: ticks
props.description: Render exactly these tick values (RM-108), bypassing generation.

props.name: domain
props.description: Pin either end of the value domain (RM-108); `"auto"` keeps the data-derived end. Read by the chart container, so place `YAxis` as a direct child. On a length encoding (bars) the domain always includes 0 — a non-zero lower bound is ignored with a dev warning (`charts-honesty`).

props.name: scale
props.description: How values map to pixels (RM-108). `"log"` refuses data or a domain that touches 0 (dev warning, renders linear); bars are linear only. Default: `"linear"`.

props.name: title
props.description: Axis title — names the unit of every tick (RM-108).

props.name: titlePlacement
props.description: `"outside"` (default) — above the top tick label in the margin; `"inside"` — `HaloText` at the top of the axis inside the plot.

props.name: labelPlacement
props.description: `"outside"` (default) — tick labels in the margin beside the plot; `"inside"` — labels sit just above their grid line inside the plot.

props.name: formatLargeNumbers
props.description: @deprecated Superseded by `valueFormat` (see `charts/value-format.ts`), which knows about millions as well as thousands — the old implementation rendered 1 500 000 as `1500k`. `false` still works and is equivalent to `valueFormat="number"`; `true` is now the default behaviour and can be dropped. Removed in the next major (`docs/DEPRECATION.md` §1).

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: How tick values are rendered. Default: `"compact"` — `1.5M`, not `1500k` and not `1500000`. Pass `"number"` for every digit.

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO 4217 code for `valueFormat: "currency"`. Falls back to `ChartConfigProvider`, then `"USD"`.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Custom formatter for tick labels. Overrides `valueFormat` entirely when set.

props.name: unit
props.description: Unit text appended to {@link unitOn} tick(s) — `<YAxis unit="%" />` paints `"80 %"` on that tick, not every tick (RM-109). The tooltip is the place a unit repeats on every value (the blog's "3.4 % unemployed", not a bare "3.4 %"); see `TooltipRow.unit`.

props.name: unitOn
props.description: Which tick(s) {@link unit} paints on. Default: `"last"`.

props.name: mode
props.description: Grid painting mode (RM-108). Default: `"lines"`.

props.name: horizontal
props.description: Show horizontal grid lines. Default: true

props.name: vertical
props.description: Show vertical grid lines. Default: false

props.name: numTicksRows
props.description: Number of horizontal grid lines. Default: the height-derived target shared with `YAxis` (`tickTargetForHeight(innerHeight)` — 3 under 200 px, else 5), so rows and labels stay aligned (RM-108).

props.name: numTicksColumns
props.description: Number of vertical grid lines. Default: 10

props.name: rowTickValues
props.description: Explicit tick values for horizontal grid lines. Overrides numTicksRows.

props.name: stroke
props.description: Grid line stroke color. Default: var(--chart-grid)

props.name: loadingStroke
props.description: Grid stroke while loading chrome is active. Falls back to `stroke`.

props.name: strokeOpacity
props.description: Grid line stroke opacity. Default: 1

props.name: strokeWidth
props.description: Grid line stroke width. Default: `CHART_HAIRLINE_WIDTH` — the one furniture weight.

props.name: strokeDasharray
props.description: Grid line dash array. Default: "4,4" for dashed lines

props.name: highlightRowValues
props.description: Horizontal row values rendered with alternate styling (e.g. zero baseline).

props.name: highlightRowStroke
props.description: Stroke for highlighted rows. Default: var(--chart-foreground-muted)

props.name: highlightRowStrokeOpacity
props.description: Stroke opacity for highlighted rows. Default: 1

props.name: highlightRowStrokeWidth
props.description: Stroke width for highlighted rows. Default: 1

props.name: highlightRowStrokeDasharray
props.description: Dash array for highlighted rows. Default: solid line

props.name: highlightRowLabel
props.description: Text label drawn at the right edge of each `highlightRowValues` entry (`HaloText`, so it survives sitting on the grid) — a KPI target/goal line the reader can name, not just see. Return `undefined`/`""` to skip the label for a given value. Unset (default): no label, byte-identical to before this prop existed.

props.name: highlightColumnValues
props.description: Vertical reference lines at these `xDataKey`-domain values (e.g. "today" on a forecast chart) — the column counterpart of `highlightRowValues`. Default: none.

props.name: highlightColumnStroke
props.description: Stroke for highlighted columns. Default: var(--chart-foreground-muted)

props.name: highlightColumnStrokeOpacity
props.description: Stroke opacity for highlighted columns. Default: 1

props.name: highlightColumnStrokeWidth
props.description: Stroke width for highlighted columns. Default: 1

props.name: highlightColumnStrokeDasharray
props.description: Dash array for highlighted columns. Default: solid line

props.name: highlightColumnLabel
props.description: Text label drawn at the bottom-inside, left of each `highlightColumnValues` entry (`HaloText`), e.g. "Today". Return `undefined`/`""` to skip the label for a given value. Unset (default): no label.

props.name: fadeHorizontal
props.description: Enable horizontal fade effect on grid rows (fades at left/right). Default: true

props.name: fadeVertical
props.description: Enable vertical fade effect on grid columns (fades at top/bottom). Default: false

props.name: yAxisId
props.description: Y-scale for horizontal grid lines. Default: primary (`"left"`) axis.

props.name: shimmer
props.description: Animate a shimmer band across horizontal grid lines. Default: false

props.name: shimmerStroke
props.description: Shimmer band stroke (color and opacity via color-mix or oklch alpha).

props.name: shimmerLength
props.description: Shimmer band width in pixels. Default: 140

props.name: shimmerSpeed
props.description: Shimmer speed multiplier (higher = faster). Default: 1

props.name: shimmerSync
props.description: Match loop timing to the loading line pulse (cycle + inter-loop pause).

stories.name: With Accessible Label
stories.description: Accessible variant — announces label + description to screen readers on focus.

stories.name: Plumb
stories.description: RM-031 — lieflat F8 "Plumb Scatter": every dot hangs a hairline "plumb line" to the floor so its x position can be read straight off the axis. Unit: sessions per day. `dropLines="x"` renders these under the markers and out of hit-testing.

stories.name: Selection states
stories.description: `selectionStates` paints the host’s tri-state on points (keyed on the datum’s region): selected marks carry a compound foreground/background outline, excluded marks dim AND carry a full-opacity dashed frame, so the three states stay distinguishable in greyscale.

stories.name: Bubble size, colour-by and a log x-axis
Bubble Size
stories.description: A 4x population draws at 2x radius (RM-039 honesty: AREA, not radius, carries the value).

stories.name: Shape By Column
stories.description: Each `team` draws with its own marker shape, not just its own colour (WCAG 1.4.1).

stories.name: With Trend Line
stories.description: A least-squares fit drawn as dashed furniture; direction/fit reach `data-trend`/`data-r2`.

stories.name: Trend line with auto summary
stories.description: With an `accessibleLabel` and no caller `accessibleDescription`, the trend's direction and r² fold into the auto summary — the text behind `aria-describedby`, read by AT, never drawn on screen.

stories.name: Trend line with a caller-written description
stories.description: The same trend, but the caller writes its own `accessibleDescription` — the auto summary (and any trend fragment) never overrides a caller's own text.

stories.name: With Custom Shapes
stories.description: Custom lines / areas (Datawrapper "custom lines & areas"): a constant `y=`, a constant `x=`, and a multi-point path — all drawn in data space, behind the marks.

stories.name: Bubble Labels Wide
stories.description: `sizeKey` doubles as the label priority by default (RM-115 × RM-110): with no explicit `labels.priority`, the biggest bubble's own `population` value decides who keeps a name when the plot cannot fit every one. Wide: most of the 40 names fit.

stories.name: Bubble Labels Medium
stories.description: The same 40 bubbles at 600px — fewer names fit than at 900px, more than at 380px.

stories.name: Bubble Labels Narrow
stories.description: The same 40 bubbles at 380px: fewer names paint, but every dropped one stays reachable through the `sr-only` restatement beside the plot.

charts/seriespattern.name: SeriesPattern
charts/seriespattern.title: Charts/SeriesPattern
charts/seriespattern.summary: Categorical comparison — composed from Bar + BarXAxis/BarYAxis inside its provider.
charts/seriespattern.about: series-pattern stories — visual + interaction surface for issue #164 (automatic high-decoration chart-series pattern fills). The demo stories are PINNED to decoration 10 (via story `globals`), so the pattern wiring renders on the ordinary shipped palettes without forcing decoration elsewhere. `NoPatternOutsideHighDecoration` pins `data-decoration="0"` to prove the gate: at decoration < 8 the charts render plain color, byte-identical to today. (Real theme-safety across the shipped themes is verified on the actual chart stories, e.g. Charts/BarChart, not these forced demos.)

intent.purpose: Categorical comparison — composed from Bar + BarXAxis/BarYAxis inside its provider.
antiPatterns: Truncating the value axis so small differences look large — a bar axis starts at zero.
Hardcoding series colors — use the chart-1…chart-5 tokens so every theme works.
Rendering an empty frame before data arrives — use the shipped chart skeleton utilities.
dataShapes: categorical comparison of one or more measures across a small set of named categories
a single signed measure around a meaningful zero, as diverging bars with a zero line
intent.avoidWhen: a time axis with many points — use a line or area chart

props.name: data
props.description: Data array - each item should have an x-axis key and numeric values

props.name: xDataKey
props.description: Key in data for the categorical axis. Default: "name"

props.name: margin
props.description: Chart margins

props.name: animationDuration
props.description: Animation duration in milliseconds. Default: 1100

props.name: animationEasing
props.description: CSS easing for bar grow transitions.

props.name: enterTransition
props.description: Motion enter transition (spring or cubic-bezier tween).

props.name: revealSignature
props.description: Signature of motion URL state — triggers enter replay when it changes.

props.name: revealOn
props.description: When the enter reveal is allowed to play (#175). `"mount"` (default) plays as soon as the chart renders — no change from today. `"inView"` holds the bars at their pre-enter state until this chart's own container scrolls to 30% visible.

props.name: replayOnClick
props.description: Clicking the chart body replays the enter reveal (#175). Default `false`.

props.name: aspectRatio
props.description: Aspect ratio as "width / height". Default: "2 / 1"

props.name: plotHeight
props.description: The plot's own height (ADR 0039): px, or `{ aspect }` (width ÷ height), optionally per breakpoint. Wins over `aspectRatio`, which stays an alias.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional class name for the container

props.name: status
props.description: Loading vs ready — shows skeleton chrome + placeholder bars while `"loading"`. Default: `"ready"`.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: Centered shimmer label while loading.

props.name: barGap
props.description: Gap between bar groups as a fraction of band width (0-1). Default: 0.2

props.name: barWidth
props.description: Fixed bar width in pixels. If not set, bars auto-size to fill the band.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Bar chart orientation. Default: "vertical"

props.name: stacked
props.description: Stack bars instead of grouping them. `true` stacks raw values; `"percent"` normalises each category to 100 % (value axis 0–100 %, a `YAxis` without its own format prints percent, `showValues` prints shares); `"diverging"` centres `divergingCenter` on the zero line with the series declared before it growing left/down and those after it right/up (Likert rows). Default: false

props.name: stackGap
props.description: Gap between stacked bar segments in pixels. Default: 0

props.name: divergingCenter
props.description: `stacked="diverging"`: the series straddling zero (e.g. `"Neutral"`). Unset: the series split in half.

props.name: stackOrder
props.description: Segment order inside each stack (`stacked`/`"percent"`). Default: `"data"` (declaration order).

props.name: showTotals
props.description: Print each stack's total just past its end. Default: false

props.name: sort
props.description: Row order: by value (`"asc"`/`"desc"`, the stack total when stacked) or `{ by, dir }`. Default: `"none"`.

props.name: reverse
props.description: Reverse the (sorted) row order. Default: false

props.name: groupBy
props.description: Gather rows by this column: horizontal bars get a bold header row per group, vertical columns a header above each group; groups are separated by a hairline and keep their own (sorted) order.

props.name: colorBy
props.description: Colour each bar by another column through `resolvePalette` (six hues, then the neutral ladder with a dev warning) and show a colour key. One key per chart (RM-118 R4): whenever this produces a non-empty colour key, the `legend` container legend below YIELDS and renders nothing — `colorBy`'s own key already covers the same job, and `interactive: "toggle"` has no effect in that mode (there is no container legend to press).

props.name: track
props.description: Paint a track behind each bar to the axis maximum ("to 100 %"). `true` uses `--chart-mono-2`, a mark-weight grey; `{ fill }` names another ink — a surface tone such as `var(--chart-segment-background)` when the track should read as paper, not as data. Default: false

props.name: overlays
props.description: Value markers and range spans drawn per bar on top of the series; listed in `legendItems`.

props.name: comparison
props.description: A muted prior-period column behind each main column (the main column narrows to make room).

props.name: comparisonLabel
props.description: Grey label beside each comparison pair. Default: `"none"`.

props.name: children
props.description: Child components (Bar, Grid, ChartTooltip, etc.)

props.name: onPhaseChange
props.description: Reports reveal lifecycle for OG screenshots and loading orchestration.

props.name: onDatapointClick
props.description: Drill-down (#349). Fires when a bar is activated by pointer OR keyboard. Setting it mounts a keyboard-operable target layer OUTSIDE the aria-hidden SVG — one tab stop, arrow keys to traverse. Unset changes nothing.

props.name: copyValueOnActivate
props.description: Put the datapoint's exact value on the clipboard when it is activated — the recovery path for a compact axis label. Default `false`; a chart with no interaction props still renders byte-identical DOM. A consumer-supplied `onDatapointClick` always wins.

props.name: datapointLabel
props.description: Override the accessible name of each keyboard drill-down target (#349).

props.name: maxInteractiveDatapoints
props.description: Dev-warning threshold on the number of keyboard targets. Default 500 (#349).

props.name: accessibleLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the chart region (announces to AT on focus).

props.name: accessibleDescription
props.description: Supplemental description read by AT (e.g. series names + value range).

props.name: palette
props.description: Default fill for `Bar` children that don't set their own `fill`, via `resolvePalette` (RM-018) over the series count — so, for example, nine unfilled `Bar` series degrade to the neutral ladder with a dev warning instead of nine bars painted identically. A `Bar` with an explicit `fill` is never touched. Default: `"categorical"` (`resolvePalette`'s own default) — but see `applyBarPalette`: it only ever assigns colours to SERIES THAT WOULD OTHERWISE COLLIDE (2+ unfilled `Bar` children), so a chart with a single unfilled `Bar` keeps today's `--chart-line-primary`.

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend engine (RM-118): `true` or a config object mounts `ChartLegend` beside the plot via `useContainerLegend`; `{ interactive: "toggle" }` turns each item into a real `aria-pressed` button that hides a series on grouped OR stacked bars — the value domain (`resolveBarValueDomain`, always zero-based) recomputes from the VISIBLE series only, and the hidden series' `<Bar>` never mounts, so it drops out of the datapoint layer too. `interactive: "hover"` (default) dims the other series via the existing `ChartLegendHoverProvider` seam `Bar` already reads. Unset renders NOTHING new (R1). Yields to `colorBy`'s own key — see its doc (R4, one key per chart).

props.name: dataKey
props.description: Key in data to use for y values

props.name: yAxisId
props.description: Y-scale group id for vertical bars (Recharts `yAxisId`). Default: `"left"`.

props.name: fill
props.description: Fill color for the bar. Can be a color, gradient url, or pattern url. Default: var(--chart-line-primary)

props.name: stroke
props.description: Color for tooltip dot. Use when fill is a gradient/pattern. Default: uses fill value

props.name: lineCap
props.description: Line cap style for bar ends: "round", "butt", or a number for custom radius. Default: "round"

props.name: animate
props.description: Whether to animate the bars. Default: true

props.name: animationType
props.description: Animation type: "grow" (height) or "fade" (opacity + blur). Default: "grow"

props.name: fadedOpacity
props.description: Opacity when not hovered (when another bar is hovered). Default: 0.3

props.name: staggerDelay
props.description: Stagger delay between bars in seconds. Auto-calculated if not provided.

props.name: stackGap
props.description: Gap between stacked bars in pixels. Default: 0

props.name: groupGap
props.description: Gap between grouped bars in pixels. Default: 4

props.name: showValues
props.description: Print each bar's value as a `HaloText` label (the `text-chart-value` role, 800-weight — lieflat G3 Chunky Bars). `true`/`"outside"` place it just past the bar's far end; `"inside"` places it just inside. A negative bar's label is signed with a "−" (U+2212, not a hyphen) glyph. A bar narrower than `MIN_LABEL_BAR_WIDTH` hides its label rather than shrinking below `text-meta`. Default: off. A {@link BarShowValuesSpec} (RM-110) adds `"auto"` placement and hover-only visibility. In a stack drawn from a layout (percent, diverging, ordered or totalled — RM-113) each segment centres its label whatever the placement, a percent segment prints its share, and a segment shorter than 24 px along the value axis stays unlabelled.

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: How `showValues` prints this series' numbers — a preset or a spec (`{ suffix: " %" }`, `{ style: "currency", abbreviate: true }`, `{ sign: "always" }`). One notation for the whole series, as without it. Unset: today's locale number. A percent stack still prints shares.

props.name: unit
props.description: Draw each bar as a countable `UnitStack` of `floor(value / unit)` rungs (vertical bars, `kind="rung"`) or ticks (horizontal bars, `kind="tick"`) instead of a solid fill — lieflat F1 Rung Bars. The rung pitch is derived from the value scale, not the bar's own pixel span, so one rung is worth the same amount in every column and the ladder never counts past the bar's own value (#241) — a value that is not an exact multiple of `unit` draws an honest partial. Width and opacity jitter via `seededRnd`, keyed per bar so neighbours never jitter in lockstep; every 5th unit draws heavier so the stack stays countable. Renders instantly (no `animate`/`animationType` grow-in). Default: off (solid fill).

props.name: highlightKey
props.description: Mark ONE bar as this series' "hero": it draws in `--chart-foreground` ink while every OTHER bar draws from `palette` instead of `fill` — lieflat's one-hero-bar-in-ink convention. A string/number is matched against the bar's category value; a function receives `(datum, index)`. Default: off (every bar draws `fill`).

props.name: palette
props.description: Palette the non-hero bars draw from when `highlightKey` is set, via `resolvePalette` (RM-018). Default: `"categorical"`.

props.name: zeroLine
props.description: Draw a 0.8px `--chart-foreground-muted` hairline at the zero baseline across the whole plot. Default: auto — shown whenever ANY bar series in this chart has a negative value; pass `false` to force it off on this series, or `true` to force it on even with all-positive data.

props.name: position
props.description: Where the tick labels sit. Default: `"bottom"`.

props.name: numTicks
props.description: About how many ticks to aim for. Default: 5, fewer when the plot is narrow.

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: How the tick values print — a preset or a spec (`{ suffix: " h" }`). Default: `"compact"`.

props.name: title
props.description: A short name for the axis, printed after the last tick ("hours").

props.name: tickerHalfWidth
props.description: Width of the date ticker box for fade calculation. Default: 50

props.name: showAllLabels
props.description: Keep every category (never stride over labels). Default: false. NOTE this no longer forces HORIZONTAL rendering: with dropping disabled the axis may still tilt, ellipsize, or hide itself when the labels cannot fit.

props.name: maxLabels
props.description: Maximum number of labels to show. Default: 12

props.name: fit
props.description: How labels that do not fit their band are rescued (RM-108): - `"auto"` (default) — horizontal → two-line `wrap` → 45° tilt → ellipsis → stride → hidden; - `"wrap"` — the same cascade without the tilt rung (never rotates); - `"tilt"` — the pre-RM-108 cascade (skips `wrap`); - `"off"` — pins the pre-fit behaviour: full labels, count-capped stride, no measurement and no reserved axis space. The regression escape hatch.

props.name: showAllLabels
props.description: Keep every category (never stride over labels). Default: true. NOTE this no longer implies every label renders in full: the axis still ellipsizes to the gutter it has, and hides itself when nothing legible fits.

props.name: maxLabels
props.description: Maximum number of labels to show. Default: 20

props.name: fit
props.description: `"off"` pins the pre-fit behaviour — full labels, count-capped stride, no measurement and no reserved gutter. The regression escape hatch. Default: `"auto"`.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: The widest the label gutter may grow, in px. The gutter is measured from the labels and capped so a long name cannot eat the plot; the default cap suits one or two words. Raise it for rows whose names ARE the content — "Send Invoice → Payment Reminder" — and the chart still keeps its own minimum plot width. Default: 112.

props.name: items
props.description: Legend items to display

props.name: hoveredIndex
props.description: Currently hovered index (for highlight effect)

props.name: onHover
props.description: Callback when an item is hovered

props.name: onItemClick
props.type: ( item: LegendItem, index: number, event: React.MouseEvent | React.KeyboardEvent, ) => void
props.description: Drill-down on a legend entry (#349). When set, each item renders as a real `<button>` — keyboard operable and named by the item's label — instead of a `<div>`. Unset, the legend is unchanged (a non-interactive `<div>` list). NOTE this lives on `ChartLegend`, not on the chart containers: the legend is a separately-placed composition primitive, so a callback on the container would be a prop the container cannot honour.

props.name: hiddenKeys
props.description: Series toggle (RM-118, `legend={{ interactive: "toggle" }}`). Set together with `onToggleKey`: every item renders as a real `<button aria-pressed>` — native keyboard support, no extra wiring — and `hiddenKeys` marks which ones read `aria-pressed="false"` and paint dimmed with a struck-through label (WCAG 1.4.1: hidden is never colour-only). Independent of `onItemClick` (drill-down); a container sets one or the other.

props.name: onToggleKey
props.type: (key: string, item: LegendItem, index: number) => void
props.description: Toggles one item's hidden state. Keyed by `item.key ?? item.label`.

props.name: hideAtDensity
props.description: Density tiers that hide the whole legend (RM-072 default: `xs`/`sm`). The container legend engine (`useContainerLegend`, RM-118) passes `["xs"]` — `sm` renders `stack`-laid-out instead of hiding — so this stays `["xs", "sm"]` for every OTHER (direct) caller, unchanged.

props.name: showProgress
props.description: Show progress bars. Default: false

props.name: showMarker
props.description: Show color marker dot. Default: true

props.name: showValue
props.description: Show numeric value column. Default: true

props.name: showPercentage
props.description: Show percentage value. Default: true when showProgress is true

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Format function for displaying values. Overrides `valueFormat` entirely when set.

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: How to format `value`/`maxValue` (RM-109) — a preset or the object form (`{ decimals, abbreviate, sign, prefix, suffix, … }`, `value-format.ts`). Resolved as a SET across every item (#250, `useChartValueSetFormatter`) so the legend never mixes "1K" beside "400". Default: locale-aware plain grouping (`intFmt`), unchanged from before this prop existed.

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO 4217 code for `valueFormat: "currency"`. Falls back to `ChartConfigProvider`, then `"USD"`.

props.name: title

stories.name: Multi Series Bar
stories.description: Three palette-fill bar series inside a `data-decoration="10"` region. Each series should render a distinct hatch pattern (diagonal / anti-diagonal / horizontal) on top of a faint ground. At decoration 0 the bars render as solid palette colors.

stories.name: Multi Series Line
stories.description: Three palette-stroke line series. Under high decoration each gets a distinct stroke-dasharray and marker shape. At decoration 0 the lines render as solid strokes with no forced markers.

stories.name: Two Series Pie
stories.description: Two-slice pie inside a high-decoration region. Each slice should get a distinct pattern fill injected via <defs>.

stories.name: Author Literal Pass Through
stories.description: A bar with an explicit hex color. Even under high decoration it must NOT receive a pattern fill (isPaletteFill returns false for literals).

stories.name: Multi Series Radar
stories.description: Two-series radar at decoration 10: each polygon area should receive a distinct hatch pattern fill injected via `<defs>`, while strokes remain solid.

stories.name: Funnel Pattern Fills
stories.description: Four-stage funnel at decoration 10: each segment's innermost ring should receive a distinct hatch pattern. The auto-inject path derives the index from the pattern id suffix (funnel-h-pattern-N / funnel-v-pattern-N).

stories.name: Sankey Node Pattern Fills
stories.description: Sankey nodes at decoration 10: each node rect should receive a distinct hatch pattern fill (applied to nodes only; links stay as gradient strokes since variable-width bezier paths with pattern strokes are illegible at thin widths — see issue #177 evaluation note).

stories.name: Composed Series Bar Pattern Fills
stories.description: Two `SeriesBar` series inside `ComposedChart` at decoration 10: each bar group should receive a distinct hatch pattern fill (diagonal vs dots), identical to the Bar resolver in BarChart.

stories.name: Pattern Id Collision Safety
stories.description: Pure logic test (no render needed): two series with different indices and the same scope must produce distinct ids; same index + same scope is stable.

charts/sparkline.name: Sparkline
charts/sparkline.title: Charts/Sparkline
charts/sparkline.summary: Tiny, axis-less trend that lives inside a KPI tile or a table cell.

intent.purpose: Tiny, axis-less trend that lives inside a KPI tile or a table cell.
antiPatterns: Adding axes and tooltips to a Sparkline — if it needs them it is a LineChart.
A Sparkline as the only carrier of a number — pair it with the value (MetricCard).
Fixing its width in pixels — let the tile or cell own the box so it reflows.

props.name: values
props.description: The series, oldest → newest.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual form. Default "bar".

props.name: emphasizeLast
props.description: Emphasize the newest value with the `--chart-1` token. Default true for bars.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name. Default describes the series (and any references below).

props.name: width
props.description: Rendered size when `fit="fixed"` (default) — the SVG's actual pixel geometry, unaffected by any CSS box the caller gives it. Also the FALLBACK size for `fit="fill"` before the first real measurement lands.

props.name: fit
props.description: Sizing strategy. `"fixed"` (default) draws at exactly `width`×`height` — unchanged no matter what CSS box (`className="w-full"`, a table cell, …) the caller puts it in, exactly as before this prop existed. `"fill"` measures the real rendered width of that CSS box (a tiny, cleaned-up `ResizeObserver`, falling back to `width` before the first measurement or where `ResizeObserver` isn't available, e.g. jsdom) and draws the plot at that real pixel width instead — no CSS stretching, so line strokes, the emphasized dot and the last-value label never distort. Opt in per usage (a trend card, a scorecard cell) rather than globally, since most Sparkline call sites size it explicitly and shouldn't pay for a measurement round-trip.

props.name: target
props.description: A horizontal reference line ("goal", "quota") drawn across the plot in `--chart-foreground`, dashed — never recolours the series even when the latest value falls short; status is the card's job, not the sparkline's.

props.name: baseline
props.description: A comparison series (e.g. last year), same index alignment as `values`. Drawn as a thin `--chart-foreground-muted` line behind the main series, in both variants.

props.name: band
props.description: A "normal range" `[lo, hi]` drawn as a quiet filled zone behind everything.

props.name: fitDomain
props.description: For `variant="line"` with no `target`/`baseline`/`band`: use the series' own min–max (padded) domain instead of the shared zero-based bar scale. A tight-range series (a weekly count moving ±5% around its own mean) reads as a flat line on a zero-based scale — decoration with no information (WCAG 1.4.1's "a channel that carries nothing" failure mode, not a colour one). Default false — byte-identical to today's shared scale when unset.

props.name: showLastValue
props.description: Render the formatted latest value as text to the right of the plot. Default false.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats every value this component surfaces as text (the last-value label and the accessible name's numbers). Default: locale number formatting.

props.name: lastValueSuffix
props.description: Appended (with a leading space) to the `showLastValue` text and to the accessible name's "latest …" phrase — e.g. `"this wk"` when the plotted series is weekly but a nearby headline figure is a different period (a quarter total), so the last-value label cannot be misread as the same fact at a different scale. Default: none (today's behaviour).

props.name: labels
props.description: Words for the reference facts in the default accessible name.

stories.name: Fill container (fit="fill")
stories.description: `fit="fill"` measures its own CSS box (here a 288px-wide container) and draws the plot at that real pixel width instead of stretching a mismatched viewBox to fit — no distorted strokes, dot or last-value label. Compare to `Default`, which stays at its fixed `width`/`height` no matter the box.

charts/tooltip-presets.name: Tooltip Presets
charts/tooltip-presets.title: Charts/Tooltip Presets
charts/tooltip-presets.summary: Hover readout for the point/series under the pointer.

intent.purpose: Hover readout for the point/series under the pointer.
antiPatterns: Putting information ONLY in the tooltip — hover content is unreachable by keyboard and on touch.
Showing every series in a shared tooltip on a dense chart — filter to the hovered series.
Formatting numbers by hand — use Intl so locale and units stay consistent with the axis.

stories.name: Rows
stories.description: Today's default box — `rows`, one row per series, byte-identical to before RM-119.

stories.name: Table
stories.description: `variant="table"` — one column per series, header row, date in the `<caption>`.

stories.name: Inline
stories.description: `variant="inline"` — no box, the hovered series' value painted at the mark (the bikes chart).

stories.name: Focus
stories.description: `focus` — the tooltip's nearest-series resolution drives RM-112's per-series dim (`SeriesHoverDim`): hovering closer to one series' line fades the other two to the shared excluded opacity. `ChartTooltip focus` registers the request on its own — no `focusOnHover` on the `LineChart` container below.

stories.name: Touch Pin
stories.description: `pin` — on a coarse pointer, a tap keeps the tooltip open after the finger lifts; a second tap, `Esc`, or a tap outside the chart releases it. `pin={true}` forces the affordance in this story regardless of the test runner's pointer type.

charts/treechart.name: TreeChart
charts/treechart.title: Charts/TreeChart
charts/treechart.summary: Fixed-spacing, left-to-right (or top-to-bottom) orthogonal hierarchy diagram — every node the same visual weight, no sizes: 'who belongs to whom'.

intent.purpose: Fixed-spacing, left-to-right (or top-to-bottom) orthogonal hierarchy diagram — every node the same visual weight, no sizes: 'who belongs to whom'.

stateTokens.linkStroke: var(--chart-grid), 1.4px — links are furniture, not data, whatever the palette
stateTokens.nodeMono: --chart-mono-1 … 7, indexed by DEPTH (the default) — every node at one depth shares one shade
stateTokens.nodeCategorical: one hue per top-level branch (a direct child of the root); the root itself stays var(--chart-mono-4), since it belongs to no branch
stateTokens.label: HaloText in the chart-value type role, placed before a leaf / after a branch on the growth axis; the halo punches from var(--chart-background)
stateTokens.collapsedPill: var(--chart-mono-3) fill, '+k' label — k is the count of leaves the pill hides
stateTokens.reveal: links draw depth by depth via DrawPath + stagger — every link into one depth shares a single reveal delay

antiPatterns: Reaching for TreeChart when the real question is 'how big is each part' — that is TreemapChart's job (leaf AREA proportional to value). TreeChart has no `value` field on TreeNode at all, on purpose: every node is the same visual weight, so it can only ever answer 'what contains what'.

Sizing or coloring a node by anything other than its DEPTH or top-level BRANCH — the two palettes are the only two encodings; a third meaning bolted onto node size or a per-leaf hue turns a membership diagram back into an unlabeled treemap.

Expecting the layout to shrink to fit its container — TreeChart lays out at FIXED node/level spacing (no ResizeObserver) precisely so it never shrinks; a tree bigger than its box scrolls inside ChartFrame instead of compressing into illegibility.

Using collapseDepth as an expand-on-click affordance — it is a static truncation (a '+k' pill with no interaction of its own); compose onDatapointClick to open a detail panel if the reader needs to reveal a hidden branch on demand.
dataShapes: a hierarchy read as a branching tree rather than as sized rectangles
intent.avoidWhen: size, not structure, is the point — use a treemap

props.name: data
props.description: The hierarchy. Every leaf needs no `value` — membership only.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `"lr"` (default) or `"tb"`.

props.name: nodeSize
props.description: Node dot diameter, in px. Default `7` (the lieflat G7 value).

props.name: collapseDepth
props.description: Render everything past this depth (root = `0`) as a single "+k" pill — `k` is the number of leaves the pill summarizes. `undefined` (default) renders the full tree, however deep.

props.name: palette
props.description: Which colour family shades a node. Default `"mono"`.

props.name: accessibleLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the chart region (announces to AT on focus).

props.name: accessibleDescription
props.description: Supplemental description read by AT.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the target group. Defaults to a localized generic name.

stories.name: Engineering
stories.description: The 40-node G7 recreation, scrolling inside a fixed 400×320 card — the acceptance bar: never shrink the layout to fit, scroll instead.

stories.name: Top To Bottom
stories.description: `orientation="tb"` — root on top, growing down; the same before/after label convention rotates onto the vertical growth axis.

stories.name: Categorical
stories.description: `palette="categorical"` — one hue per top-level branch; the root stays neutral since it belongs to no branch.

stories.name: Collapsed
stories.description: `collapseDepth={1}` — every branch past depth 1 collapses into a single "+k" pill, `k` = the number of leaves it hides.

stories.name: Interactive
stories.description: Click a node — or Tab in and press Enter — to report it below.

charts/treemapchart.name: TreemapChart
charts/treemapchart.title: Charts/TreemapChart
charts/treemapchart.summary: Two-level squarified treemap — a hierarchy where area, not position, encodes value.

intent.purpose: Two-level squarified treemap — a hierarchy where area, not position, encodes value.

stateTokens.band: var(--chart-mono-2) — always neutral, even under palette: 'categorical', so grouping reads from the title band + gap alone, never from hue
stateTokens.leafMono: var(--chart-mono-4) — one shared shade for every leaf (the default)
stateTokens.leafCategorical: one hue per top-level group (≤ 4 groups, else falls back to mono)
stateTokens.label: HaloText: the band title renders in the chart-source type role, the leaf label in the chart-value type role (RM-019, both pinned to the meta size step); the halo punches from var(--chart-background)
stateTokens.focus: the drilldown zoom/back buttons carry the shared compound focus indicator (--ring plus the --ring-contour outline), shown only on keyboard focus

antiPatterns: Comparing a leaf's area against a leaf in a different group — area is only comparable WITHIN one parent's total; two leaves under different groups are fractions of different denominators, so their tile sizes are not commensurate across the group boundary.

Reaching for palette: 'categorical' to encode a second measure on top of area — the hue there still only labels the group a leaf already belongs to (structurally, via the band); asking it to carry an unrelated variable makes one channel do two jobs and defeats the mono default's greyscale-legible design.

Leaving a long tail of small leaves unmerged until tiles fall below labelMinArea — set otherThreshold before that happens (the unconditional 30-leaf cap is a backstop, not a substitute for tuning it); a treemap of unlabeled slivers reads as noise, not a breakdown.

Turning on drilldown as the only way to reach a leaf's value — the group-band zoom button is a SEPARATE affordance from onDatapointClick on purpose; a leaf stays selectable by its own click/Enter without first forcing a reader to drill in.
dataShapes: a nested hierarchy sized by one measure
intent.avoidWhen: the hierarchy has fewer than 2 levels — a flat bar chart is clearer

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the target group. Defaults to a localized generic name.

stories.name: Mono
stories.description: Default palette: one shared neutral shade per leaf — groups read apart only by their title band + paper gap, so the chart stays legible in greyscale.

stories.name: Categorical
stories.description: One hue per top-level group (≤ 4 groups); leaves inherit their group's hue.

stories.name: Sequential
stories.description: Leaf shade encodes the leaf's own value on the sequential ramp.

stories.name: Legend, categorical groups
stories.description: One row per top-level group, colour-keyed to the same hue each group's leaves/title band paint. Hovering a row dims every OTHER group's tiles.

stories.name: Legend, sequential ramp
stories.description: `palette="sequential"` has no discrete key — it renders the shared `RampLegend` instead.

stories.name: Depth: 1 (flat)
stories.description: Flat, single-level rendering — root's children only, no title bands.

stories.name: Other Threshold
stories.description: A long tail of small leaves merges into a single "Other" tile once each falls below 5% of its group's total.

stories.name: Show Values
stories.description: `showValues` (#247) prints each tile's value under its name, so the quantity survives a screenshot, an export and a keyboard user — not only a hover. A tile too short or narrow for the whole number keeps its name and drops the value; values share one notation across the set. Off by default.

stories.name: Show Values Other Threshold
stories.description: The folded "Other" tile with its value printed — how much the long tail adds up to.

stories.name: Drilldown
stories.description: Click (or Tab to and press Enter on) a group's title band to zoom into it; the "← Work" control zooms back out. This is a SEPARATE affordance from `onDatapointClick` — the static stories above have no click handler beyond it.

stories.name: Interactive
stories.description: Click a leaf — or Tab in and press Enter — to report its datum below.

stories.name: Selection states
stories.description: `selectionStates` paints the host’s tri-state on leaf tiles: selected marks carry a compound foreground/background outline, excluded marks dim AND carry a full-opacity dashed frame, so the three states stay distinguishable in greyscale.

charts/unitchart.name: UnitChart
charts/unitchart.title: Charts/UnitChart
charts/unitchart.summary: One mark = one honest unit — waffle grid, phyllotaxis field or tick rows, so a share is COUNTED rather than judged by angle or area; lieflat's default replacement for a pie.

intent.purpose: One mark = one honest unit — waffle grid, phyllotaxis field or tick rows, so a share is COUNTED rather than judged by angle or area; lieflat's default replacement for a pie.

stateTokens.marks: fill/stroke resolved per series from the active ChartPalette (--chart-1.. or the mono ladder past 6 series) — never a raw hex
stateTokens.leader: field's cluster-to-label callout is a 0.6px var(--chart-foreground-muted) dashed hairline — furniture, never a second data channel
stateTokens.caption: text-caption in var(--chart-label) for unitLabel, var(--chart-foreground-muted) tabular-nums for the arithmetic remainder
stateTokens.rowValue: rows' value at the inked edge is var(--chart-foreground) at font-weight 800 — the one heavy mark in the row

antiPatterns: Sizing a waffle or field past a few hundred marks in a small frame — UnitStack already warns that one stack stops being countable past ~60 units; here the same failure happens across the WHOLE canvas at once, so budget total/columns/frame size together, not one series at a time.

Turning showArithmetic off (or padding a count) because a rounded-away caption looks untidy — the caption exists BECAUSE the chart never invents a mark to hit total; hiding it trades the one honest-count promise this chart makes for a tidier footer.

Reaching for layout="field" when the reader needs to rank two series or compare them precisely — a phyllotaxis cluster reads as an area-at-a-glance impression, not a countable structure; a real comparison wants rows or waffle, where the grid gives the reader something to count.

Falling back to a pie chart because comparing shares 'still feels easier' to build — that instinct is exactly what this chart exists to correct: a slice angle cannot be counted, a mark can. If the categories genuinely don't sum to a meaningful whole, reach for the rows layout, not a pie.
dataShapes: parts of a whole as discrete unit counts rather than a percentage, as layout="waffle"
one tally row per category, ticks summing to a total — ticket volume by weekday, for example, as layout="rows"
intent.avoidWhen: exact per-unit counts do not matter — a pie or bar chart reads faster

props.name: data
props.description: The series — one labeled quantity per row.

props.name: layout
props.description: Which lieflat layout to draw.

props.name: total
props.description: What 100% of the marks represents. Default 100 (percent). Ignored by `rows`.

props.name: unit
props.description: Value per mark. Default 1 — a `unit={2}` chart draws one mark per two incidents.

props.name: unitLabel
props.description: "one dot = one person in a hundred" — rendered as a caption and folded into the a11y summary.

props.name: columns
props.description: Grid columns for `waffle`. Default 10.

props.name: mark
props.description: Mark shape for `waffle`/`field`. Default `"dot"`.

props.name: palette
props.description: Color family. Default categorical; degrades past 6 series (RM-018).

props.name: showArithmetic
props.description: Show the footer arithmetic ("41 + 35 + 12 + 12 = 100 · 2 rounded away"). Default `true`. Ignored by `rows`.

props.name: sort
props.description: Sort series by value, descending, before laying out. Default `"none"` (caller order).

props.name: accessibleLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the chart region.

props.name: accessibleDescription
props.description: Supplemental description read by AT.

props.name: items
props.description: Legend items to display

props.name: hoveredIndex
props.description: Currently hovered index (for highlight effect)

props.name: onHover
props.description: Callback when an item is hovered

props.name: onItemClick
props.type: ( item: LegendItem, index: number, event: React.MouseEvent | React.KeyboardEvent, ) => void
props.description: Drill-down on a legend entry (#349). When set, each item renders as a real `<button>` — keyboard operable and named by the item's label — instead of a `<div>`. Unset, the legend is unchanged (a non-interactive `<div>` list). NOTE this lives on `ChartLegend`, not on the chart containers: the legend is a separately-placed composition primitive, so a callback on the container would be a prop the container cannot honour.

props.name: hiddenKeys
props.description: Series toggle (RM-118, `legend={{ interactive: "toggle" }}`). Set together with `onToggleKey`: every item renders as a real `<button aria-pressed>` — native keyboard support, no extra wiring — and `hiddenKeys` marks which ones read `aria-pressed="false"` and paint dimmed with a struck-through label (WCAG 1.4.1: hidden is never colour-only). Independent of `onItemClick` (drill-down); a container sets one or the other.

props.name: onToggleKey
props.type: (key: string, item: LegendItem, index: number) => void
props.description: Toggles one item's hidden state. Keyed by `item.key ?? item.label`.

props.name: hideAtDensity
props.description: Density tiers that hide the whole legend (RM-072 default: `xs`/`sm`). The container legend engine (`useContainerLegend`, RM-118) passes `["xs"]` — `sm` renders `stack`-laid-out instead of hiding — so this stays `["xs", "sm"]` for every OTHER (direct) caller, unchanged.

props.name: showProgress
props.description: Show progress bars. Default: false

props.name: showMarker
props.description: Show color marker dot. Default: true

props.name: showValue
props.description: Show numeric value column. Default: true

props.name: showPercentage
props.description: Show percentage value. Default: true when showProgress is true

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Format function for displaying values. Overrides `valueFormat` entirely when set.

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: How to format `value`/`maxValue` (RM-109) — a preset or the object form (`{ decimals, abbreviate, sign, prefix, suffix, … }`, `value-format.ts`). Resolved as a SET across every item (#250, `useChartValueSetFormatter`) so the legend never mixes "1K" beside "400". Default: locale-aware plain grouping (`intFmt`), unchanged from before this prop existed.

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO 4217 code for `valueFormat: "currency"`. Falls back to `ChartConfigProvider`, then `"USD"`.

props.name: title
props.description: Title shown above the legend

props.name: layout
props.description: Item flow direction (RM-118, sitting 3). `"stack"` (default — every caller before this prop existed) is byte-identical to before: one item per line. `"row"` wraps items left-to-right (`flex-wrap`), matching the layout `AutoChart`'s old `AutoLegend` used, AND drops the `w-full` an interactive (`onItemClick`/toggle) item otherwise gets — `w-full` inside a row would force every item onto its own line regardless of this prop. `useContainerLegend` (the container legend engine) passes its own resolved `layout` ("row" at `base`/`medium`/`wide`, "stack" at `narrow` or density `sm`) through; a direct caller may set its own or leave it unset for the original stacked behaviour.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional class name for the container

props.name: titleClassName
props.description: Class name for the title

props.name: itemClassName
props.description: Class name for each legend item

props.name: labelClassName
props.description: Class name for the label

props.name: valueClassName
props.description: Class name for the value

props.name: renderItem
props.type: (props: { item: LegendItem; index: number; isHovered: boolean; isFaded: boolean; percentage: number; }) => ReactNode
props.description: Custom render function for legend items

stories.name: Default
stories.description: Waffle — column-major grid, one dot per unit (lieflat's "G4 Dot Waffle").

stories.name: Field
stories.description: Field — golden-angle phyllotaxis cluster per series (lieflat's "L14 Hundred Field").

stories.name: Rows
stories.description: Rows — one tick row per series, ticked every 10 (lieflat's "L15 Ballot Tally"). Rows may sum past `total`.

stories.name: All Layouts
stories.description: Waffle / Field / Rows side by side — the acceptance's cross-layout comparison.

stories.name: Rounding Remainder
stories.description: The rounding rule: a series that does not divide evenly into `unit` never invents a mark — the footer calls out the shortfall instead ("98 · 2 rounded away").

stories.name: Mark Shapes
stories.description: `mark="square"` and `mark="tick"` — the two alternates to the default dot.

stories.name: Outline Variant
stories.description: A per-datum `variant: "outline"` draws that series hollow (stroke only, no fill) — a second channel beside colour for "this is the one series that matters" (WCAG 1.4.1), and it keeps a quiet majority from visually dominating a highlighted minority the way a solid dark fill would. Default (`variant` unset) stays a solid fill, unchanged.

stories.name: Performance Stress
stories.description: 1,000 marks across 5 series. The per-mark reveal is a plain CSS `transition-delay` computed once in JS (`unitMarkDelayMs`) — never a per-mark `motion`/framer-motion component — so this stays a single paint regardless of mark count. See `unit-layouts.ts`'s stagger constants.

stories.name: Drilldown
stories.description: Click a series — or Tab in and press Enter — to drill into it. One keyboard target per series, never per mark.

stories.name: Selection states
stories.description: `selectionStates` paints the host’s tri-state on each category’s marks: selected marks carry a compound foreground/background outline, excluded marks dim AND carry a full-opacity dashed frame, so the three states stay distinguishable in greyscale.

charts/waterfallchart.name: WaterfallChart
charts/waterfallchart.title: Charts/WaterfallChart
charts/waterfallchart.summary: Gross-to-net bridge: running-total steps and subtotal bars showing what added and subtracted along the way.

intent.purpose: Gross-to-net bridge: running-total steps and subtotal bars showing what added and subtracted along the way.

stateTokens.connector: var(--chart-foreground-muted), 0.6px, dashed (furniture, not data — Leader's default)

antiPatterns: A `total` row whose value does not actually equal the running total at that point — the connector into it visibly plunges/jumps instead of landing flat, which is the bridge silently telling you the reconciliation is wrong.
Reading the dashed connector as if it carries a value — it is furniture that hands off between steps, never a series; the story is the bar heights, not the connector's slope.

Entering a reduction as a positive `value` (or otherwise fighting the sign convention) — color and the +/− label are derived from the actual before/after delta, not from caller intent, so a flipped sign silently mislabels the step.
More than ~6-8 steps in one bridge — past that the running total stops being followable and the connectors turn into visual noise; split into a top-level bridge plus a drill-down instead.
dataShapes: a running total with signed steps into and out of it
intent.avoidWhen: there is no meaningful running total — use diverging bars instead

props.name: data
props.description: Steps from gross to net — one row per bar.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Default `"vertical"`.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Signed value label on each step (`HaloText`, 800 weight). Default `true`.

props.name: connectors
props.description: Dashed hand-off hairline between each step's end and the next step's start: `false` draws none, `true`/`"thin"` the default weight, `"thick"` a heavier one (RM-122). Default `true`.

props.name: dataFormat
props.description: `"differences"` (default): `data` values are signed deltas. `"runningTotals"`: every row's `value` is the running total AT that row — converted once, up front (RM-122 `waterfall-steps.ts`).

props.name: subtotalBy
props.description: Auto-inserts a `kind: "subtotal"` checkpoint after each run of rows sharing this field's value (RM-122) — e.g. `subtotalBy="quarter"` with `{ label, value, quarter: "Q1" }` rows. Off by default.

props.name: subtotalLabel
props.description: The inserted subtotal row's label — a `"{group}"` template. Default `"{group} subtotal"`. Ignored without `subtotalBy`.

props.name: sort
props.description: Reorders `"step"` rows within each subtotal group (RM-122). Default `"data"` (spreadsheet order).

stories.name: Default
stories.description: Gross → refunds → COGS → ops → net: connectors hand off at the running total, totals draw from zero, labels are signed.

stories.name: Horizontal
stories.description: Same data, horizontal orientation — the label-fitting `BarYAxis` plan.

stories.name: Unit Rungs
stories.description: `unit` renders each bar as a counted `UnitStack` of rungs — the F9 look — instead of a solid capsule. The pitch comes from the value scale, so one rung is worth the same amount in every step (#241) — stated here since the waterfall renders no axis of its own to read it from.

stories.name: With Callouts
stories.description: `callouts` names the one or two steps that actually explain the bridge — drawn above the step with a `Leader`, so a reader does not have to infer "which of these five bars is the story" from height alone. Needs extra `margin.top` for the note's own headroom.

stories.name: No Connectors No Labels
stories.description: Connectors and value labels can both be turned off for a quieter read.

stories.name: Drilldown
stories.description: Click a step to drill into it; the detail panel below reports the datum.

stories.name: Keyboard Drilldown
stories.description: The same drill-down reached with the keyboard only — one tab stop for the whole chart, ArrowRight to traverse every step, Enter to activate.

stories.name: Running Totals
stories.description: `dataFormat="runningTotals"` reads every row as the running total reached at that point instead of a signed delta — the same bridge as `Default`, converted once on the way in.

stories.name: Quarterly Subtotals
stories.description: `subtotalBy` auto-inserts a subtotal checkpoint after each run of rows sharing that row field's value — here, one after every quarter's months.

stories.name: Sorted Decreases First
stories.description: `sort="decreasesFirst"` reorders the steps WITHIN each subtotal- or total-bounded group — the checkpoints themselves never move.

stories.name: Zoomed To Differences
stories.description: `zoomToDifferences` drops the zero baseline when a checkpoint sits far above the steps' own swing — a `"total"`/`"subtotal"` row can no longer honestly draw as a zero-based bar once zero is off-screen, so it renders as a point on a dashed stem instead; the steps themselves stay ordinary bars, since a delta's length is proportional under any linear domain.

stories.name: Percent Difference Labels
stories.description: `labels` with `differences: "percent"` reads each step as a signed percent of the running total it left off, instead of its absolute value — `matchColor` paints each label in its own row's ink (through `seriesLabelInk`, never the raw fill, #544) instead of the neutral halo ink; the mixed increase/decrease/subtotal rows exercise the `layoutLabels` collision pass (RM-122) against both the annotation and axis obstacles.

stories.name: Thick Connectors
stories.description: `connectors="thick"` weights the hand-off hairlines for a bolder read.

props.name: attributions
props.description: The notices to render. Defaults to the GENERATED dataset (`scripts/gen-attributions.mjs`), which is what keeps this panel accurate without anyone maintaining a list — override only to scope or to test.

props.name: categories
props.description: Restrict to these categories, in the panel's own order. Default: all.

props.name: packages
props.description: Restrict to notices reachable through these packages — e.g. an app that only uses `…-ui` need not credit MapLibre's basemap providers. Matched against each entry's `usedBy`. Default: all.

props.name: requiredOnly
props.description: Show only the notices a licence obliges us to display.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Cap the body height and scroll inside it. Omit to let the panel grow and leave scrolling to the container (a Dialog body, a settings pane).

stories.name: Default
stories.description: The full generated dataset, scrolling inside a fixed height.

stories.name: Required Only
stories.description: The minimum a product must display: only the notices a licence obliges. This is the variant to mount when screen space is tight — a footer "Attributions" link or an About dialog section.

stories.name: Scoped To Maps
stories.description: Scoped to one package — what an app that only renders maps has to credit.

stories.name: Source And Fonts
stories.description: Adapted source and fonts only — the provenance half, without the dependency tail.

stories.name: Empty
stories.description: A filter that matches nothing still renders a real empty state, never a blank box.

intent.purpose: Compact status/label chip (status, count, category).
antiPatterns: Using it to carry an execution status — that is StatusBadge, whose closed seven-state vocabulary pairs a distinct glyph with every tone so the state survives greyscale.
Using a Badge as a clickable control — use a Button (Badge is not interactive).
Encoding status by color alone — pair the color with text/icon for non-color users.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Explicit per-instance override of the fill/border/ink treatment. Unset (default) renders NO `data-appearance` attribute, so the badge is driven purely by the ancestor `--badge-appearance` token (`auto` = each variant's own recipe, today's look). Meaningful only on the colour-bearing variants (`default`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`) — see `badgeVariants`.

stories.name: Appearances
stories.description: The four explicit `appearance` overrides (`tint`/`solid`/`outline`/`neutral`) on every colour-bearing variant — each renders a `data-appearance` attribute and a fixed fill/border/ink recipe regardless of the ancestor `--badge-appearance` token. `secondary`/`outline` are already a neutral pill and an outline respectively, so `appearance` has no additional effect there.

stories.name: Token Driven Appearance
stories.description: With no explicit `appearance` prop, an ancestor's `--badge-appearance` token (a theme, or a region wrapper) drives the treatment instead — the badges below carry no `data-appearance` attribute at all.

components/ui/button.name: Button
components/ui/button.title: Core/Button
components/ui/button.summary: Primary action trigger — the canonical way to invoke an action.

intent.purpose: Primary action trigger — the canonical way to invoke an action.

avoidNextTo: another primary Button

stateTokens.focus: focus-ring — the compound indicator: a ring-2 in --ring plus a 1px --ring-contour outline (#67) + ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background

Button used for navigation — use a link instead (asChild + <a>, or the variant="link").
destructive variant for an irreversible action with no confirm step — wrap in AlertDialog.
Icon-only Button without an aria-label — the control has no accessible name.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the child element as the button (Radix Slot) instead of a <button>.

stories.name: Keyboard focus (WCAG 1.4.11)
stories.description: #67 — the RENDERED lock on the compound focus indicator (ADR 0027 Amendment). A class-string assertion would be worthless here: `focus-ring` could name a single-layer ring and the class would still be present while the ratio stayed at 1.36:1, which is the exact failure this story exists to prevent. So this play function measures the SHIPPED pixels — it reads the computed indicator layers off a really-focused button, resolves the ground the indicator is actually drawn on by walking up to the first non-transparent ancestor, and asserts at least one layer clears WCAG 1.4.11 (3:1) against it. It is theme-agnostic on purpose: whichever theme the run resolves (the toolbar global, or `STORYBOOK_THEME=<slug>` headless — see @.claude/rules/storybook-mcp.md § Themes) the SAME assertion has to hold, so one story covers `light`, `dark` and any consumer theme a fork adds.

components/ui/card.name: Card
components/ui/card.title: Core/Card
components/ui/card.summary: Surface grouping related content into a bordered, padded block.

Card-for-everything — use a Card only when a bordered surface is the right affordance.
Identical icon-tile-above-heading Card grids repeated endlessly — vary structure.

Use `hover` for **supplementary** detail only — essential content must use `fixed`. @default "fixed"

props.name: as
